about: What may differ between BN5's battle (the reference) and BN6's with a family moved in (the subject), and why: tools/xdiff.py reads each game's numbers as BN6's (maps), each game's structures through their own layouts (layouts), and replays BN6's draws from BN5's by the twins of its rng, the engine's own draws one game alone makes named there too (rng), and lets a difference pass only where a mask names it (masks), each an engine difference that is not the family's code, with the evidence: both games' routines by address. No mask applies to the family's own records (its objects, what they own, its attacks and effects): what the engine writes there in its own numbers is read as BN6's in the snapshot, as an enemy id is (maps: alliance, renderer, slot), and any other difference there fails the spec (docs/multirom/families.md; docs/devtools/differential.md). No game code here: addresses and numbers only.

name_id.why: An object's NameID (+0x28) is its enemy id: BN5's CanGard family is 0x4F-0x54, moved as BN6's ids 0x200-0x205, and its Handi family 0x13-0x18 as 0x206-0x20B, the families' (src/emu/xvirus_families.c, .first_id; xvirus_recipe.h, XV_FIRST_ID); BN5's Navis by their recipes (src/emu/xnavi_bn5.c, .first_id; src/emu/xnavi_recipe.h, XN_ID_OF): ToadMan's V1-SP 0x143-0x146 as 0x1D8-0x1DB, KnightMan's 0x13D-0x140 as 0x1D4-0x1D7, ShadowMan's 0x12B-0x12E as 0x1C8-0x1CB, NumberMan's 0x131-0x134 as 0x1CC-0x1CF, TomahawkMan's 0x137-0x13A as 0x1D0-0x1D3, Colonel's 0x125-0x128 as 0x1C4-0x1C7, the Dark Soul's 0x18D as 0x1DC, the Darkloids ShadeMan's 0x149-0x14C as 0x1E0-0x1E3 and BlizzardMan's 0x14F-0x152 as 0x1E4-0x1E7, CosmoMan's 0x15B-0x15E as 0x1EC-0x1EF and CloudMan's 0x155-0x158 as 0x1E8-0x1EB, Team ProtoMan's NapalmMan's 0x113-0x116 as 0x1FC-0x1FF GyroMan's 0x107-0x10A as 0x1F4-0x1F7, SearchMan's 0x10D-0x110 as 0x1F8-0x1FB and Meddy's 0x11F-0x122 as 0x3E8-0x3EB; MegaMan is 0x180 in BN5 and 0x1A0 in BN6 (his battle object's NameID in both traces from their first frame).

megaman_forms.why: MegaMan's NameID in a form of BN6's is 0x1AB + the form (0x08015B22 writes it as he crosses: 0x1AC-0x1C3; 0x1A0 in none), where BN5's stays 0x180 through a Soul and its end (the research's runs/nid). His role is MegaMan's whatever his form; his NameID is compared as BN6 writes it for the form BN5's maps to (a Soul behind the proxy, 0x1B3).

chip_id.why: A chip id: BN5's by the chip registry's rows (src/core/xchips_registry.c: a chip both games name alike BN6's id, BN5's other chips the ids of their own), read from the source the game is built from, as BN6's engine has them in its tables (docs/multirom/chip-registry.md). Translated where an object keeps one: a battle object's chip (+0x2A, BN6_T1_CHIP, the chip it uses next, u16, 0xFFFF none: written as the hand deals it to MegaMan and as a virus picks its own) (a virus's held chip picked, or its own code's: Zomon's AreaGrab), and the AI data's places below (its AttackVars +0x14, the chip used, written by the chip's use, BN5 0x0800FF68 / BN6 0x08012824, and by a virus's chip writer, BN5 0x0800FE7C / BN6 0x080126F6: strh r0,[r7,#0x14], r7 the AI data + 0xA0). A virus's CurAction from 0x10 that is the family the chip writer returned for its chip (the record's +0x0B, BN5 0x0800FEBA / BN6 0x0801273A, for setAttack0) is read as BN6's family of BN6's chip (tools/xdiff_snap.py, chip_action): the same chip in each game's own numbers. And where a support chip's routine keeps it: its object's +0x30 (r7 as the support family calls the routine: the chip used, its AttackVars +6 above it; BN5 0x080EC416 / BN6 0x080ED0F8), by the object's type (t4: the fourth kind's). The support chips' objects keep it so: each spawned by its support routine with r7 the chip (and AttackVars +6 above it), stored at +0x30 (MetaGel's 0x21, Blinder's 0x23, Jealousy's 0x36, NrthWind's 0x39, BoyBomb's 0x67, RainyDay's 0x75, BlakWing's 0x54, HolyDrem's 0x59, HotBody's 0x57, the Anti chips' setter 0x2A and its counter 0x2B (spawned by BN5 0x080E38E2 as its trap springs), DarkCirc's 0x5E and DrkSonic's 0x4A (chip_darkcirc, chip_drksonic: 0xBB and 0xC6 there in BN5's, BN6's ids 0xD6 and 0xDC), RockCube's 0x37 (BN5's chip 99, BN6's 143: BN5 0x080E47CE / BN6 0x080E59F6, twins) and Poltrgst's 0x72 (BN5 0x080E8DC2, moved: chip_poltrgst, 213 in BN5's, the registry's 292 in BN6's): their routines BN5 0x080E2F84, 0x080E3228, 0x080E4628, 0x080E493C, 0x080E816E, 0x080E91EE, 0x080E6AB4, 0x080E6F60 HotBody's family 0x080F0222 and the Anti chips' 0x080E380A (0x080E3828), each str r7,[r0,#0x30]); and the third kind's: the Anti chips' trap 0x4D, its setter's chip passed on (BN5 0x080CF7F4: str r7,[r0,#0x30]). A virus's support chip (its held chip's family 0x15 by the chip writer, Zomon's AreaGrab) runs BN5's support family's timing in BN6's engine as family 0x65 (src/emu/xvirus_dispatch.c's XV_SUPPORT: BN6's 0x15 run twice in one frame, the attack ending in its routine's frame as BN5's 0x080EC448 ends it; the families' calls to BN5's chip writer, 0x0800FE6A, aimed at XV_CHIP_WRITER, which gives 0x65 for 0x15): its CurAction BN5's 0x15 read as 0x65 (virus_support), MegaMan's and a Navi's own 0x15 BN6's (tools/xdiff_snap.py, chip_action).
evidence: DarkInvs's object (BN5's fourth kind's 0x18, spawned by its support routine 0x080E2420: str r7,[r0,#0x30], the chip used) keeps its chip at +0x30 as the support objects of BN6's do (chip_darkinvs: BN5's 189, BN6's 289)

zomon_v1 t1: Zomon's +0x2A 0x75 in BN5's (its set-up's movs r0,#0x75; strh r0,[r5,#0x2A], BN5 0x08108932-0x08108934: chip 117, AreaGrab) and 0xA3 in BN6's (163, AreaGrab: the registry's row 117 to 163, SAME); t390 its AttackVars +0x14 the same chip, its CurAction the chip's family 0x15 by each game's record (BN5 0x0801E210 + 0x2C x 117, BN6 0x08021DA8 + 0x2C x 163, +0x0B 0x15 in both)

PileDrvr's object (BN5's fourth kind's 0x6F, spawned by its support routine 0x080E8994: str r7,[r0,#0x30] at 0x080E89B2, the chip used) keeps its chip at +0x30 as DarkInvs's does (pa_piledrvr t33: BN5's 349, the registry's 604)

zomon_v1: setAttack 0x15 in BN5 and 0x65 in BN6 at t390, Zomon's state back in both at t391 (BN6's 0x15 alone ended it at t392); BN5 0x080EC400-0x080EC448, BN6 0x080ED0DC-0x080ED130 (phase 1: 0x08011714)
chip_id.subs_why: Where an object keeps its chip's subfamily beside the chip (subs, by the object's type: the bytes, a word's low byte, that hold it), BN5's is read as BN6's of BN6's chip (behaviour6: its record's, or the moved code's entry), where it is BN5's record's (+0x0C). The Navi chip's object, the fourth kind's 0x10, spawned by the Navi family's routine (BN5's family 0x41 at 0x080EC458, BN6's 0x1B at 0x080ED690, the same steps) through its spawner (BN5 0x080E1AC0, BN6 0x080E2C6C): the AttackVars' subfamily (+3) its +0x3C, the spawner's ldr r1,[r0,#0x3c]; strb r1,[r0,#0x19] (BN5 0x080E1AEC-0x080E1AEE) its +0x19 too, and the chip (+0x14, +6 above it) its +0x30; a Navi chip moved as BN5's Navi routine S runs as BN6's 0x1D + S (chip_numbrman: 0 as 0x1D, chip_shadoman 0xB as 0x28, at t33)

code_twins.why: A routine's address an object keeps (a Thumb pointer into each game's own code) is the same routine where both games' routines are twins: the same instructions but for the calls' targets, each game's own twin. Listed by pair, each pair's bodies compared (pairs). And a moved family's code may keep a routine of BN5's engine as a callback (its attack's variables +0x28, a jump table of its own): the install names BN6's twin there (the recipe's words). The snapshot reads such a word of BN5's as the twin the family's recipe gives it, where BN6's word is that twin: a translation by the recipe's pairs, each pair's bodies compared by tools/xrecipe.py (the same, the same but for the offsets of loads and stores, or a differing pair its audit takes, bn5_twins.AUDITS); a word aimed elsewhere in BN6 stays a difference.
evidence: tests/xdiff/families.json, code_twins: each family's pairs, written by tools/xrecipe.py with src/emu/xvirus_bn5.c
flashy_v1, powie_v1: the attack's callback BN5 0x08012A21 / BN6 0x08015C49 and BN5 0x08012A6D / BN6 0x08015C95, each family's recipe's pair
pairs: AreaGrab's and PanlGrab's support routine (subfamily 0 in both: BN5's table 0x080297BC, BN6's 0x0802CCB4): its spawn of the fourth kind's type 3 leaves the routine's address, the support family's r3, in its object's +0x3C (the spawner keeps r1-r4 as the object's words)
BN5 0x080E08D8-0x080E08F9 / BN6 0x080E1B1C-0x080E1B3D: the same 17 instructions but for the spawner's call (BN5 0x080031CC / BN6 0x080033AC, the fourth kind's)
Geddon's support routine (BN5's subfamily 4, BN6's 3): its spawn of the fourth kind's type 0x1D leaves the routine's address in its +0x3C as AreaGrab's does
BN5 0x080E286E / BN6 0x080E38A6: the same instructions but for the calls' targets (tools/xrecipe_thumb.py compare: SAME)
RockCube's support routine: its spawn of the fourth kind's type 0x37 leaves the routine's address in its object's +0x3C as AreaGrab's does
BN5 0x080E47CE-0x080E47EF / BN6 0x080E59F6-0x080E5A17: the same 17 instructions but for the spawner's call (BN5 0x080031CC / BN6 0x080033AC, the fourth kind's)

ai_index.why: AIData +1, the AI index the engine finds a family's tables by: CanGard's 14 in BN5, 32 in BN6's grown tables; Handi's 4, 33 (xvirus_cangard and xvirus_handi .src_ai, .ai).

t3_type.why: An attack's type (+1), by its number in BN5 where BN5's is moved: BN6 spawns a moved type of the family's (CanGard's reticle, BN5's third kind's type 0x25) as the second-level dispatch's type of its kind (the first's 0x5C, the third's 0xD2, the fourth's 0x91: xvirus_recipe.h, XV_T*_DISPATCH), its BN5 number in the kind's side table by the object's slot (BN6_DISPATCH_SIDE: the first kind's at 0x0203FF00, the third's at 0x0203FF20, the fourth's at 0x0203FF40), and the dispatch runs it as that number. The trace writes the side table's byte beside each object of a dispatch type (src/dev/xdiff.c, version 3) and the snapshot reads its type as that byte (tools/xdiff_snap.py): a translation, not a mask, so a moved type keeps its BN5 number in both and is the same. The spawn hook reads the dispatch's spawner's frame the same way (its BN5 type and its caller, src/dev/xdiff_events.c). A twin of BN6's is spawned as BN6's own number, and mapped here where the numbers differ: BN5's lance (the misc family's subfamily 4, DrkLance's over its twin BN6's Lance) is its third kind's 0x4F, BN6's the same code at its 0x6F.
evidence: the dispatch's spawner (src/emu/xvirus_dispatch.c, the project's own Thumb): push {r0,lr}; TWIN by the type's low byte; XV_TYPE_MOVED spawns the kind's dispatch type; after BN6's spawner, the type into the side table at the object's slot (+3); its frame above BN6's spawner's five words: the type at +0x1C, its caller at +0x20
the dispatch type's routine: ldrb r0,[r5,#3]; the side table's byte; MOVED's routine for it, r1 the type times four as BN5's runner leaves it (BN5 0x08003014-0x0800301E / BN6 0x080031F4-0x080031FE)
BN6's runner reads +1 alone and its spawn writes it alone (BN6 0x080031F4, 0x080032BE); the moved code never reads it (the installer refuses ldrb rX,[r5,#1] in a moved block)

the lance: BN5's third kind's 0x4F (0x080CF938) and BN6's 0x6F (0x080D3CD0) the same instructions (tools/xrecipe_thumb.py's compare: SAME), spawned by each game's misc subfamily 4 (BN5 0x1A, BN6 0x1C, the registry's DrkLance twin 119); chip_drklance

effect.why: An effect object's id (+4 of the fourth kind's type 0): CanGard's muzzle blast is BN5's 0x57, copied as BN6's 0x6C (the immediate at BN5 0x08108FB6). The Navis' own effects take numbers from 0xA0, the Navis' range, one a BN5 effect whichever Navi (or the sea's marker, tools/bn5_objects.py) spawns it (src/emu/xnavi_bn5.c, its effects: tools/xnavirecipe.py), and an effect BN6 draws alike is BN6's (Colonel's 0x47, his strike's: BN6's 0x60, list 4's 0x0A the same bytes as BN5's list 4's 0x2C, its animation and palette 0, tools/xrecipe.py's effect_twin), read so only where a spec's foes hold one of its ids (navis): BN5's engine and its other enemies spawn those BN5 ids for effects of their own (the Mettaur's 0x14), each compared as BN6's of its number. BN5's sea's splash (0x63, a non-Aqua object stepping onto sea: BN5_PANEL_ARRIVED) is BN6's 0xAC wherever it is spawned, the moved objects' copy (tools/bn5_objects.py, ENGINE_EFFECTS; src/emu/xsea.c spawns it). The Souls' (the Souls track's S4, tools/xsoul.py) share the other tracks' copies: ColonelSoul's ScreenDivide's three, BN5's 0x48-0x4A (its family 0x43's base 0x48 + its sub-family, BN5 0x080EEE18), are the Navis' 0xA8-0xAA, TomahawkSoul's swing 0x45 the Navis' 0xA6, ShadowSoul's slash 0x17 (its sword family's sub-family 2, BN5's table 0x080EC112) the Navis' 0xA3: BN6 has an effect of the same record (0x17, and 0x33 for 0x45: its list, number, animation and palette) whose sprite, redrawn, animates for other frames, and an effect lives as long as its animation (copies).

copies.why: In a spec with the Souls installed (souls6), or whose spec asks (effect_copies: the obstacle strike's, colonel_strike): BN5's effects the Souls' code spawns that BN6's engine spawns of its own too (0x14 and 0x02, BN6's redrawn: 0x02 by a counter's family 0x47, BN6's twin of BN5's 0x2C), and ShadowSoul's slash 0x17 (BN6's of the same record redrawn, another animation), run as the Navis' copies of BN5's (one BN6 number a BN5 effect, issue #82's allocations: 0xA0, 0xA2, 0xA3, src/emu/xnavi_bn5.c), and the Souls' own copies, 0x03 (the unison's phase 0 spawns BN6's own) at 0xC0 and the obstacle strike's shot's hit 0x20 (its table 0x080C6C08, row 12, fixed in the chips' copy: tools/bn5_twins.py's SHARED_ROWS) at 0xC1, each drawn with BN5's sprite: a BN6 copy is read as the BN5 effect it copies, BN5's id as itself in both (which of the two a spawn is, the code that spawned it says). ColonelSoul's ScreenDivide's three (0x48-0x4A) and TomahawkSoul's swing (0x45) are the Navis' 0xA8-0xAA and 0xA6, read as such in every spec (tools/xdiff_snap.py's chip_effects, the chips' units naming them). The Navis' 0xAB, Colonel's copy of BN5's 0x01, the same: in colonel_strike BN6's engine spawns its own 0x01 where BN5's spawns 0x01, and Colonel's code the copy.

flash.why: A muzzle flash (the first kind's type 5, spawned by BN5 0x080B9CAE / BN6 0x080BA6A0 with its number in r4, kept at +4) is drawn by the entry of that number in each game's table of flashes, 5 bytes each (BN5 0x080B9A5C, BN6 0x080BA444, read at BN5 0x080B9BA8 / BN6 0x080BA570: its list, sprite, animation and palette): BN6 numbers the same flash otherwise. Each pair here names the same entry, or the same picture (the sprites byte for byte) at another number of list 3. The image object's own kinds, BN5's object moved once for every track (tools/bn5_objects.py: the Navis' images, the chips' muzzle flashes, the Souls' arm flashes and MegaMan's buster's in a Soul, src/emu/soullook.c), keep BN5's numbers in both games, the one copy run through the second-level dispatch: compared as they are (ob.moved).
evidence: BN5's entry 0x09 and BN6's 0x15: 0C 19 00 00 0B (list 3's 0x19, animation 0): Spreader's flash (BN5 0x080EC5B4's family, BN6 Spreadr1's 0x25)

BN5's entry 0x11 (0C 2A 00 00 0C) and BN6's 0x23 (0C 59 00 00 0C): list 3's 0x2A in BN5 (0x08314EBC) and 0x59 in BN6 (0x08348D44), the same 1216 bytes: WideSht's flash (BN5 0x080ED0BE movs r4,#0x11; BN6 0x080EE8CA movs r4,#0x23, the same family routine but for it)

soulcode_bn5.c's types (1, 0x05 moved, BN5 0x080B9B81) and bytes (the kinds 0x03, 0x0A, 0x23, 0x31, 0x32 and 0x33 their sprites as BN6 lists them); soul_colonel's t203: ColonelSoul's flash kind 3 in both

panel_type.why: A panel's type (+2), the type it is drawn as (+6, the one-frame override's at +8) and the low nibble of its flags (BN5's +0x18, BN6's +0x14, the type ORed into its table's word): BN5's lava (8) and sea (0xA) are BN6's free types 13 and 14 where src/emu/xpanels.c brings them in, BN5's holy (9) BN6's 5 (src/emu/xfields.c), the rest the same numbers.
evidence: the flags: _object_updatePanelParameters ORs the type into its word, BN5 0x0800AFE0 / BN6 IWRAM 0x030078DC (ldrb r1,[r0,#2]; ... orrs r1,r3)

the drawn type: the same routines copy +2 to +6; BN5's per-panel update writes lava's 8 or 2 there as it blinks (0x0800AA68), BN6's its conveyors' own type or 2 (0x0800C478), the path lava and sea take in BN6 (xpanels.c, panel_ages)
the flags' words: lava's 0x11010 and the sea's 0x30010 are BN5's (BN5_PANEL_FLAGS_OF), copied into BN6's grown table (xpanels.c, flags_make)

alliance.why: A collision data's +0x30 (what it is) and +0x34 (what it strikes) are words the engine's setup takes from a table by the object's alliance and a region its caller names, two words a region, and ORs the time stop's bit 0x10000 into +0x30 while time is stopped; each game has its own table (layouts, collision, alliance_masks), whose entries mostly differ by BN6's bit 0x80. So a BN5 word is read as the BN6 entry at its place in BN5's table (with the time stop's bit as it is): over the 160 entries each BN5 word gives one BN6 word (a word two entries would give otherwise would be left as it is; none does). A hit and a touch OR the other object's +0x30 into what hit or touched it (BN6's +0x70 and +0x6C, BN5's +0x68 and +0x64): such a word is read as the OR of the BN6 words of the table's words it is made of, where every way of making it gives the same (else it is compared as it is), its bit 0x01 as it is: the hit pass's own where an attack struck a guard, no table word's. Not the family's code: the setup and the hit pass are the engine's, and the family's region and alliance are compared through them (a family object set up with another region reads as another BN6 word). A BN5 word two places give otherwise, BN6's with bit 0x80 at one and without at the other (BN5's 0 is BN6's 0 at region 0 and 0x80 at others), is read as BN6's where BN6's is either: the place is the setup's own (its r1 and r2), which no trace records.
evidence: the setup: BN5 0x08016760-0x080167AE / BN6 0x08019FB4-0x0801A00C, the same steps: +0x30 from the table's reader (BN5 0x08016BBC / BN6 0x0801A0BA: alliance x 4 + region x 8) for the region in r1, stored at BN5 0x0801678A / BN6 0x08019FE8; 0x10000 ORed in where the time stop's test (BN5 0x08008A78 / BN6 0x0800A098, bit 2 of the battle's flags) is set (BN5 0x08016792-0x0801679C / BN6 0x08019FF0-0x08019FFA); +0x34 for the region in r2 (BN5 0x080167A6 / BN6 0x0801A004)

the tables (layouts, collision, alliance_masks): BN5 0x08016364 reads 0x08410000, 0x04210000, 0x80000000, 0x40000000 (entries 2, 3, 8, 9) where BN6 0x08019C7C reads 0x08410080, 0x04210080, 0x80000080, 0x40000080; entries 4-7, 10, 11 alike in both; of BN5's 160 words 128 have their BN6 entry with the bit, 30 the same word, region 61's two (BN5 0x80000080, 0x40000080) BN6's 0x80

the hit pass ORs the hitter's +0x30 into what hit it: BN5 0x080169E8-0x080169F2, 0x08016A28-0x08016A34 (its +0x6C/+0x70, then +0x68) / BN6 0x081D7800-0x081D7804, 0x081D783A-0x081D7840 (+0x70); the second pass into what touched it: BN5 0x080174AA-0x080174B0 (+0x64) / BN6 0x081D7BD2-0x081D7BD8 (+0x6C)
BN6's use of its bit: its second pass lets an object whose +0x3C has 0x20 touch only one whose +0x30 has 0x80 (0x081D7BAE-0x081D7BD0); BN5's twin 0x0801748C has no such test

in the traces of every spec each +0x30 and +0x34, and each hit and touch word on the frames compared, reads as its BN6 word: MegaMan's 0x08410000, CanGard's and the Mettaur's 0x04210000, the reticle's 0x40000000, MegaMan's shots' 0x80000000, each with 0x80 in BN6; a reticle's hit word 0x08410000 (MegaMan's) as 0x08410080

the guard's bit: where the struck object's +0x3C has bit 0x01 (guarding: KnightMan's) and the attack's +0x30 has neither of 0x1002, the hit pass ORs 1 into what hit the attack: BN5 0x080169B0-0x080169CA (its +0x6C + 4 x the struck's side) / BN6 0x081D77C4-0x081D77E2 (+0x70); none of the 160 words of either table has bit 0x01 (their low bits are 0x02-0xA0); knightman_v1_keys' buster shot at t39 on KnightMan guarding: BN5's 0x04210001, BN6's 0x04210081

renderer.why: Each frame the sprite renderer hands each object it draws a place for its tiles in OBJ VRAM (its sprite state's +0x08, u16) from a running count over all it draws before it, and a palette slot (+0x15's high nibble) from the slots taken before it; a frame or palette already loaded this frame is given its place or slot again. The code is the same in both games, but what each draws (MegaMan's own sprite, his flash and sparks, BN6's own effects, a native) differs, so the numbers do. A family object's place and slot are read as their rank among those the family's objects drawn that frame take: the family's own draw order and sharing, compared; what else is drawn among them is no part of the family's. One not drawn (its +0x00 bit 0x02 clear, its sprite's state's +0x03 bit 0x02 clear: the renderer's own test, as an object can hide its sprite alone; or its cache, +0x24, clear: the renderer passed it over, NumberMan's companion while visible) keeps the place it was last drawn at, so it keeps that rank; one whose place moved undrawn is compared as it is; one never drawn has no place the renderer gave it (its sprite state holds its slot's last occupant's, or its set-up's; its spawn clears its record short of them): none, in both. Slot 15 (none taken) stays. The frames the family draws are compared from its sprite's own data (+0x1C, +0x20) and its cache (+0x24), so its tile counts are. The same places of what is not the family's are masked (the renderer's slots, the renderer's palette slot). A family object whose place (or slot) in BN5 is one an object not the family's draws that frame (the renderer keeps a frame or palette already loaded where it is: the Dark Soul's buster's arm and muzzle, 3:0x03 and 3:0x06, the same art as BN5's MegaMan's own, which BN6's MegaMan draws from BN6's) is ranked in neither game, read as shared in both (tools/xdiff_masks.py, SHARED).
evidence: the renderer: BN5 0x081C7F26-0x081C804C and BN6 0x081D64BE-0x081D65E4 (the IWRAM renderer's ROM copies), the same code but for their literal pools

a sprite's state not shown is skipped, its cache cleared and its place kept: BN5 0x081C7F9A-0x081C7FAC / BN6 0x081D6532-0x081D6544 (ldrb [r5,#3]; tst #2); metfire_v1: the fire column's object shown and its sprite not (t199-t203, t317-t321), its place the one it was last given (BN5 29, BN6 59), and a column's place before its first draw its slot's last occupant's (t247: BN5 59, BN6 29)

the tile place: BN5 0x081C7FF4-0x081C7FFC / BN6 0x081D658C-0x081D6594, the running count's value stored and the frame's tiles added to it (BN6 0x081D6562-0x081D6566, 0x081D6590-0x081D6594); a frame already copied this frame is given its place again (found at BN6 0x081D66A8-0x081D66C6, stored at 0x081D65B8); a sprite not drawn keeps its old place, its cache cleared (BN6 0x081D653A-0x081D6544)

slot.why: An object's header +3 is its slot in its kind's array, which the engine hands out to the first free one. Objects are matched by role (what they are, in the order they appeared), never by slot, so +3 is read as counted from the object's own slot: 0 where it is its own, as the engine writes it, so a slot taken in one game and not the other (an effect living a frame longer) is no difference of the object's.
evidence: the slot is the first free bit of the kind's bitmap: BN5 0x080030B4-0x080030C2 / BN6 0x08003294-0x080032A2 (the same code); the spawn clears the object from +4 on (BN5 0x080030CC-0x080030D2 / BN6 0x080032AC-0x080032B2) and writes +0 and +1, leaving +3 as the slot holds it
in both traces of cangard_v1_keys every object's +3 equals its slot (5856 objects in BN5's, 5822 in BN6's)

action.why: CurAction (+9). A virus's: BN5 numbers generic states 0-5 and its own from 6, BN6 generic 0-7 and its own from 8 (two status states, frozen and bubbled, between), so BN5's 0-5 are BN6's 0-5, its 6 BN6's 8, 7 on two up (every family table in both ROMs; the attack's end writes 6 at BN5 0x0800F2E2 and 8 at BN6 0x08011754). MegaMan's: ready 6 in BN5, 8 in BN6 (BN5_MEGAMAN_READY, BN6_MEGAMAN_READY), his others the same (a step 0x10, hit 3, seen in both traces). The same numbering holds for an attack of the third kind that runs the same states: its state table BN5's generic 0-5 and its own from 6, BN6's 0-7 and its own from 8 (t3_types; Handi's obstacle, the third kind's type 0x4B, run by BN5 0x08017FCC / BN6 0x0801B394 from its state table BN5 0x080CF118, 8 entries, BN6 0x080CF264, 10: its own 6 and 7 BN6's 8 and 9; the bomb BomBoy throws and BoyBomb sets, the third kind's 0x3E, its update BN6's twin 0x080CD4A8 in the one copy both run, the chips', from BN6's table: bomboy_v1 its bomb's 6 in BN5 and 8 in BN6 at t19; the cube a RockCube stands, the third kind's 0x59, run by the same routine from BN5's table 0x080D117C, 7 entries, BN6's 0x080D12B8, 9: chip_poltrgst its own 6 in BN5 and 8 in BN6 at t33; "0x59 twin": only where BN6's object runs BN6's own type, Colonel's moved copy of it keeping BN5's numbers, colonel_sp). MegaMan's actions of a family (CurAction from 0x10, run from each game's table of families, BN5 0x080EB514, Gregar 0x080EBFA0) by the twin of each: BN5's 0x1A, the Soul's unison and its end (the player update 0x08014604 sets it from AIData +0x44's bits 0x4000 and 0x40), is BN6's 0x1C, the Cross's and Beast Out's (its twin 0x08017BC0, the same steps); BN5's 0x1E, the plain charged shot (0x080ECAB8), is BN6's 0x16 (0x080ED140), the same phases but BN5's first: it tests the battle's flag 0x40 (0x080ECAE0) and fires at once where it is clear, where BN6's always waits 5 frames first (0x080ED168), so a charged shot parts the two games (no spec fires one: docs/devtools/differential.md). The step (0x10), the buster (0x11) and the Cannon's (0x14) are the same number in both. The first kind's +0x5D is a CurAction too, read the same way: a status saves the object's state word (+0x08: +0x09 its CurAction) at +0x5C as it takes it and restores it as it ends (the paralysis's, BN5 0x0800CB84-0x0800CB8C / BN6 0x0800E76C-0x0800E774, then CurAction 4; the restores, e.g. BN5 0x0801384E / BN6 0x0801575C: ldr r0,[r5,#0x5C]; str r0,[r5,#8]). A foe's attack family (CurAction from 0x10, run from each game's table of families) is the same number in both where BN6's family of that number is BN5's (the step 0x10, which the Dark Soul's moves take, 0x0800F280 / 0x080116F6), and BN5's family F that BN6 has none of, moved with the Navi that runs it, BN6's 0x50 + F in the grown table (families; src/emu/xnavi_recipe.h, XN_FAMILY_OF): the Navis' buster, BN5's 0x16, as 0x66; a virus's own action of a chip's family by its chip (chip_id). A Soul's charged shots run as the families the Souls track moved (S4: BN6's attack families grown, xattack_grow.c, the Souls' from 0xC0 in tools/xsoul.py's FAMILIES' order): BN5's 0x43 (ColonelSoul's) BN6's 0xC0, 0x3A (NumberSoul's) 0xC1, 0x40 (KnightSoul's) 0xC2, 0x50 (ToadSoul's) 0xC3, 0x3D (ShadowSoul's B+Left) 0xC4, 0x45 (TomahawkSoul's) 0xC5, and 0x13 by his attack (megaman_by_attack). A counter's two families (a hit taken in ShadowSoul's B+Left stance: BN5's 0x2C and 0x2D, twins of BN6's 0x47 and 0x48, started by BN5's 0x0800E338 and BN6's 0x080105F2, whose family's first frame the Souls' Thumb runs at once as BN5's: src/emu/soulcode.c's counter_code) are BN6's 0x47 and 0x48. A failed Chaos Unison's family (BN5's 0x39, 0x080EE724: the Dark Soul spawned, MegaMan out of the Soul) is BN6's 0xC7, Chaos Unison's Thumb (src/emu/soulchaos.c; xattack_grow.h's Souls' range), the same phases. BN5's family 0x49 (0x080EF270, the player's answer to his request 0x80000: BN5's DarkInvs's end, its time at 0, and Slasher's reaction) runs moved as BN6's 0x99 (the chips' Reaction49; src/emu/darkinvs.c starts it where BN6's twin starts BN6's own family 0x49, another: chip_darkinvs_end).

megaman_by_attack.why: Under BN5's chip AI (DarkInvs's machine, src/emu/darkinvs.c: his AI data +0xF0 1 while it is under way, which BN5 clears every other idle frame, 0x0802C03E) MegaMan fires the Navis' buster (BN5's setup 0x3E, 0x0800FAFE: family 0x16), as the Dark Soul does: BN6's engine runs BN5's family 0x16 moved with the Navis (XN_STUB_BUSTER, tools/bn5_navi_twins.py FAMILIES) as 0x66 (xnavi_recipe.h's XN_FAMILY_OF)

sound.why: A sound is compared by its song number: the music player it plays on is its song table entry's, each game's own (song 0x6A, MegaMan's buster's, is BN5's player 22 and BN6's player 0; the reticle's 0xAE player 4 in both). A song each game plays on another player (players_apart: 0x6A, the buster's, which BN5 plays for MegaMan's buster and the Navis' alike and BN6 for MegaMan's, the Dark Soul's taking BN6's: tools/bn5_navi_twins.py, SOUNDS_AS_BN6) begins or not as its own player there is free (BN5's player 22 busy with MegaMan's charged shot's 0x6B, BN6's player 0 free): asked for in both games in a frame (their sound events, which are compared as the family's calls), it is left out of the songs begun. A copy of BN5's sound in one of BN6's empty slots (src/audio/xsong.c: the families' packed into their own room and noted, the Navis' copied there, one slot a sound whichever track copies it) is read by BN5's number in BN6's trace (xsong_copy_of), so the copy is BN5's song; in a spec whose foe is a moved Navi, BN6's own song of a number a copied sound of BN5's has (0x70, 0xB7, ...) carries bit 16 and is never read as BN5's (a Navi's code plays every sound of its from the copy); in a family's, BN6's own song of the number is the engine's, a twin of BN5's routine playing each game's own by its number (0x70, which Bugtank's thrown bomb and MetFire's fire column play from their state routines' twins, BN5 0x080C93B8 / BN6 0x080CA1B6 and BN5 0x080D0DB0 / BN6 0x080D0D88, called through their jump tables: bugtank_v1 t178, metfire_v1 t169; each game's song of the number differs). The Souls' sounds go the same way (tools/xsoul.py's SONG_SLOTS: BN5's 0x70 at 0x5F, 0x117 at 0x5E, 0x115 at 0x5A, src/emu/soulpower.c through xsong_install_at), read by BN5's number.
evidence: the song tables: BN5 0x08155BF4, BN6 0x08159F48 (RomLayout.song_table), 8 bytes a song: its header, its player

family_effects.why: Effects (the fourth kind's type 0) name no object that spawned them; those of the effect ids the family's code spawns are the family's, compared as such: its muzzle's blast (BN5's 0x57, BN6's 0x6C: BN5 0x08108FB6) and its reticle's strike (0x0E: BN5 0x080C9660-0x080C9662); a Navi's, its own (effect, navis: 0xA0 on). Any other effect is the engine's or another enemy's (in the smoke spec the Mettaur's 0x14), which stops a spec as MegaMan's own state does.

rom_tables.why: A pointer into each game's own ROM is read by the data there (32 bytes the same: a table both games have). Where a table's end is followed by other bytes in each game, the 32 bytes from its last entries run past it: such a table is named here, by its place in both and its entries' size and count, and a pointer into it is read as its place in it, the entry there the same bytes in both (else the entry differs, and so does the pointer).

sprites.why: A sprite is compared by what it is, not by where each game keeps it: a sprite state's data pointer (+0x18, the sprite's start + 4) named by the registry's pair, the same list and entry of each game's sprite lists (BN6's RomLayout.sprite_lists 0x08031CC4, BN5's XRomLayout's 0x0803272C: a word per list, a word per entry). Where either game's pointer is one of a pair's, both must be that pair's: MegaMan drawn from another sprite, his flash or a spark another, is a difference. A sprite of no pair (a moved family's, BN5's from its battle's cache in EWRAM) is compared as before, its frames from its own data; where a spec says "sprites": "bytes" (every moved family's), one of no pair in both games' ROMs, or a family's copy (tests/xdiff/families.json's art), is compared by its bytes, the same picture where the same bytes (tools/xdiff_snap.py, sprite_sha), as the generator's twins are: a type of BN6's drawing other art than BN5's is a difference.

WideSht's muzzle flash (the same 1216 bytes in both)
Spreader's muzzle flash (each game's own picture)

power_attack.why: MegaMan's AI data +4 to +8 and +0x11 name his power attacks (his charged shot's at +7, BPwrAtk), each an entry of each game's table (BN5 0x0800F368, 108 entries; Gregar 0x080117D4, 148, grown by the Souls track's S4 to 159 in the Souls' room and by S6 to 165, soul_room.h's SOULS_POWERS, the word 0x080117D0 pointed at the copy): BN5's number read as BN6's. In both games his plain loadout is ff ff 00 01 ff ff (no Cross, no Soul: the normal charged shot, entry 1 of each, BN5 0x0800F5B4 and Gregar 0x08011A7E, 10 x (Attack + 1)), and 0xFF none: the same numbers. A Soul's are BN6's from SOUL_POWER_FIRST (0x94) in the recipe's order (tools/xsoul.py's POWERS: ColonelSoul's charged shot 0x14 and chip shot 0x13, ShadowSoul's charged shot 0x17 and B+Left 0x45, NumberSoul's 0x07, TomahawkSoul's 0x1A, KnightSoul's 0x11, ToadSoul's 0x2D), then the three whose BN5 routine is the empty one, their charge times alone read (the A button's chip charge: 0x12, 0x18, 0x1B); then a Soul's Chaos Unison attack (+0x11, every Soul's loadout's sixth: the Souls track's S6, src/emu/soulchaos.c), in soulpower.c's chaos_powers order: ColonelSoul's 0x3A (DrkSonic), ShadowSoul's 0x31 (DarkInvs), NumberSoul's 0x32 (DarkPlus), TomahawkSoul's 0x33 (DrkLance), KnightSoul's 0x38 (DarkDril), ToadSoul's 0x34 (DarkWide), their routines Chaos Unison's Thumb, each the chip writer of the Soul's DarkChip in BN6's ids (BN5's 0x0800FA36-0x0800FA98), their charge times BN5's rows (40, 60, 90, 120, 150 by the level).
evidence: src/emu/soulpower.c's tables(): the grown table, BN5's rows of 0x0801CA18 by the Soul written in BN6's ids into SOULS_LOADOUTS, the loadout's read (0x0800FEEC) hooked to them for the proxy form with a Soul; soulcode_bn5.c's powers

souls.why: A Soul's state: BN5 keeps it in MegaMan's AI data (its turns +0x0F, its chaos +0x12, the chaos charge's cycle +0x1C and phase +0x1F, ColonelSoul's chip +0x32, 0xFFFF none, the chaos level +0x6C) and names the Soul by his form byte; BN6's engine keeps it in the Souls' block (BN6_SOULS, a side's 0x20 bytes: +0 the Soul, +1 chaos, +2 turns, +3 phase, +4 the chip, 0 none, +6 level, +0x16 the cycle, +0x10 the Souls used this battle, +0x14 ColonelSoul's chip committed at OK, 0 none), as BN6's AI data has its own fields at those places (+0x0F a turn guard, +0x12 the HP bug's level, +0x32 tired). So BN5's AI data reads 0 at those places (its Soul's state compared here instead), its used word (BN5_SOULS_USED) against the block's, and BN6's Crosses' used word must be 0 (BN5 has no Cross). BN5's battle mood (his battle NaviStats' +0x0E) is compared with the block's +0x0E, BN5's mood as BN6's engine keeps it by BN5's rules beside its own (the Souls track's S7, src/emu/soulmood.c), from the battle's first Custom screen; BN6's own mood is compared as before (maps, the mood less BN5's gains). The block's other bytes are BN6's engine's own bookkeeping (+7 the opening's mood set, +0x0F the dark latch, +8-+0xA the Soul committed and not yet entered, +0xB element 0xB's role, +0xC what stands under OK): not compared. Element 0xB (UNITE, BN5_CUSTOM_UNITE and BN6_CUSTOM_UNITE) is compared byte for byte as each game's last Custom screen left it. ColonelSoul's chip committed at OK (his button's, BN5's Custom record's +6 copied into his pending record's +6, 0xFFFF none) is compared with the block's +0x14 (0 none), both in BN6's chip numbers by the spec's folders.

dispatch_copy.why: BN6's virus dispatcher (each virus each frame, the first kind's type 0 for enemies) writes the virus object's +0x3E into its AI's data +0x3C after its state has run, but while it is bubbled (its CurAction 7, a state BN5 lacks); BN5's dispatcher writes nothing there. So a moved family's AI data reads BN6's dispatcher's copy at +0x3C where BN5's keeps whatever its own code left (nothing, for every family moved so far). The snapshot reads BN5's +0x3C as BN6's dispatcher writes it, its object's own +0x3E, where BN5's +0x3C is 0 (its code wrote none): a translation of the family's record, not a mask; where BN5's own code wrote a value there it is compared as it is.

collision.why: A collision data is 0xA0 bytes in BN5 and 0xA8 in BN6, laid out otherwise from +0x14: each segment is (BN5's offset, BN6's, bytes), found by pairing the two games' routines (the symbol map's pairs whose instructions agree but for an offset on a register loaded from an object's +0x54) and checked against both traces. Where one game keeps in two bytes or words what the other keeps in one, BN5's parts are checked by their rule (bn5_or: the word BN5 ORs them into, which is compared with BN6's); a byte of either outside the segments and the rules must be zero in both. The flag words (flag_words, BN6's offsets) hold bits, never addresses, so they are compared as bytes even where they look like a ROM address.
evidence: +0x00-0x13 the same: the paired routines' accesses at +1, +2, +6, +9, +0xA, +0xB, +0xC, +0xD, +0xE, +0xF, +0x10, +0x11 agree (e.g. BN5 0x08016B64 / BN6 0x0801A050, the collision panels' update); the setup BN5 0x08016760 / BN6 0x08019FB4 writes +1, +2, +4, +7, +0xA, +0xE alike

BN5 +0x1A is BN6 +0x16: BN5 0x080EAB64 / BN6 0x080EB550, a u16 read after the barrier (+6)

alliance_masks.why: The words the setup stores at +0x30 and +0x34 come from this table, by the object's alliance and its region (two words a region): BN5's 160 words (80 regions; BN5_COLL_MASKS, BN5_COLL_MASK_WORDS) against the first 160 of BN6's 178 (89 regions; BN6_COLL_MASKS, BN6_COLL_MASK_WORDS). Each BN6 word is its BN5 twin with bit 0x80 or as it is, but region 61's (entries 122 and 123: BN5 0x80000080 and 0x40000080, BN6 0x80 and 0x80); tools/xdiff_snap.py checks this as it reads them. table_words are the collision data's words set from the table (with the time stop's bit), or_words those ORed of other objects' table words (a hit's, a touch's), at BN6's offsets: each read as BN6's (maps, alliance).
evidence: the readers: BN5 0x08016BBC / BN6 0x0801A0BA (alliance x 4 + region x 8 into the table, its one literal at BN5 0x08016C00 / BN6 0x0801A0D0); the setup's stores BN5 0x0801678A, 0x080167A6 / BN6 0x08019FE8, 0x0801A004
the tables' ends: code follows at BN5 0x080165E4 and BN6 0x08019F44 (the same routine in both, push {r4,r6,r7,lr})

a word ORed of them holds the hit pass's own flags too, bits no table word of either game has (their 160 and 178 words together 0xFFFDFFBE: 0x1, 0x40 and 0x20000 none's), kept as they are: bit 0 ORed into what hit an object (BN5 0x080169BE-0x080169CA into +0x6C or +0x70 by the hitter's side / BN6 0x081D77DC-0x081D77E2 into +0x70), 0x20000 with the hitter's word (BN5 0x080169E4 / BN6 0x081D77FC); bladia_v1_keys t516: MegaMan's shot struck by Bladia, its word 0x04310001 in BN5's (+0x68 and +0x6C) and 0x04310081 in BN6's (+0x70), Bladia's table word 0x04310000 / 0x04310080 and bit 0

bn6_slips.why: BN6's hit-clear (0x0801A018, a frame's hits taken from an object's collision data) means to keep the hits of a time stop at +0x54 (it ORs +0x54 and +0x70 into r0) but stores r1, its caller's leftover (0x0801A022: str r1,[r4,#0x54]), and clears it once time runs again: a slip of BN6's engine, in a word no moved code names (BN5's twin keeps its own there, the hits ORed, 0x08016B30). Compared nowhere: as a support chip is used, the battle stands still a frame (the support family's 0x0800BF16, BN5's 0x0800A50A) and every object's +0x54 holds that leftover for it.
evidence: BN6 0x0801A01C-0x0801A022: ldr r2,[r4,#0x70]; ldr r0,[r4,#0x54]; orrs r0,r2; str r1,[r4,#0x54]; then 0x0801A032 clears it where the time stop's test (0x0800A098) is clear
chip_areagrab: CanladEX's +0x54 4 in BN6's alone at t33, the frame AreaGrab's support routine runs

panel.why: A panel is 0x24 bytes in BN5 and 0x20 in BN6: +0x00-0x0F the same (type +2, alliance +3, the state the panel's update keeps at +0x0E), BN5's alliance timer +0x12 BN6's +0x10 (the alliance's setter, BN5 0x0800B2D6 / BN6 0x0800CC14: strh at +0x12 / +0x10), the flags BN5 +0x18 / BN6 +0x14 (BN5_PANEL_FLAGS, BN6_PANEL_FLAGS; the panel's parameters read there, BN5 0x0800AFB0 / BN6 0x0800C8F8), +0x1C / +0x18, and the object holding it BN5 +0x20 / BN6 +0x1C (the panel's reservation, BN5 0x08018654 / BN6 0x0801BB1C)

timers.why: BN5 keeps a timer for lava (+0x10) and one for the sea (+0x14), each 0x3C0 while its panel is another (written every frame, and as the field is made), counted down while it is lava or sea; BN6 keeps one (+0x12), 0x708 on most panels, counted down on a conveyor, and on lava and sea as BN6's engine runs them (src/emu/xpanels.c: from 0x3C0, BN5's, as each is made). So where one of BN5's two is not 0x3C0 it is that panel's timer, compared with BN6's +0x12 (on the frame lava cools under an object both still hold the count the update left); where neither is, the masks for their idle values hold. On the frame lava or the sea runs out BN5's reads 0 (its update ends the count, plain, and writes 0x3C0 the next frame) where BN6's reads 0x708 again (its conveyors' count writes it as it ends): the same.
evidence: BN5: the field made, 0x0800AB66-0x0800AB70 writes 0x258 to +0x0E, 0x3C0 to +0x10 and +0x14; the update counts lava's +0x10 (0x0800AA4C) and the sea's +0x14 (0x0800AA78) down to plain, each other branch writing 0x3C0 to the other

BN6: the field made, 0x0800C564 writes 0x708 to +0x12; the update counts it down for 9-12 (0x0800C45C) and for 13 and 14 by xpanels.c's hook at 0x0800C3B8, which sets it to 0x3C0 where it still holds 0x708; object_setPanelType's hook (0x0800CC0A) gives a chip's lava or sea 0x3C0, as BN5's 0x0800B2A6 does
the count's end: BN5 0x0800AA56-0x0800AA64 (lava) and 0x0800AA82-0x0800AA90 (sea) set the type plain and +0x0E, the timer left at 0; BN6 0x0800C466-0x0800C474 sets it plain and writes 0x708 to +0x12

sea.why: BN5's sea's submerge (bn5.h: BN5_SEA_TEST, BN5_SEA_SUBMERGE, BN5_HIDE_STEP): BN5 keeps it in the object's collision data, its +0x2C 0xFFFF while it stands on sea with its traits' bit 0x20, its flag 0x80000000, and the marker that follows it at +0x50. BN6's engine has no submerge (its bubble took the flag and the timer, +0x50 its invisibility's marker), and the port keeps it apart (src/emu/xsea.c, RAM_SEA: the mask of the submerged collision data's own bits, BN6_COLL_INDEX_BIT, then their markers by that bit's index; the trace's apart bytes). BN5's read as the port keeps it: the timer and the flag out of the record, the flag compared with the mask, the marker with the port's by what each names.

BN5 0x0800DEB0-0x0800DED0: flags & 0x80000004 clear the object's visible bit and spawn the marker (0x080E4D1E) into +0x50 (str r0,[r4,r7], r7 0x50) where none, else end it (0x080E4D36) and clear +0x50
BN6 0x0800E820-0x0800E832: +0x2C its bubble's timer, counted down, flag 0x80000000 cleared with it at 0 (0x0801A15C); its hide step 0x0801012C (+0x50 its marker) called by nothing
toadman_sp at t657: ToadMan SP under on the sea his own attack made, BN5's +0x2C 0xFFFF, flag 0x80000000 and its marker at +0x50, the port's mask and marker the same

pointer_bytes.why: Bytes an object's own code writes from a pointer's low bytes (an AI data's byte, a moved object's coordinate), read by it only as such: compared as the pointer they came from (byte k of the word at `pointer` in the same record, read as what it names), each game's objects at their own addresses. part: 'ai' an enemy's AI data by its BN5 ids; 'obj' an object of a kind and type (BN5's number, a moved type's in both records).

rules.evidence: KnightMan's state 11 (BN5's 9), its sub-state 0x10 (BN5 0x080FC08C): ldr r0,[r7,#0x28] (AttackVars +0x28: his companion's overlay, the first kind's 0x56); bl 0x080C386C (BN6 0x080C5D80, the same bytes: its +0xB cleared, r0 returned as it came); strb r0,[r7,#1] (BN5 0x080FC0AA): the phase's flag the overlay's address's low byte, tested only as nonzero (0x080FC090). The overlay in T1 slot 2 in both traces: 0xB0 in BN5, 0x60 in BN6 (0x0203A9B0 + 2 x 0xD8).

NumberMan's number box (the third kind's 0x8B, moved, its type BN5's number in both records): his state at BN5 0x080FA5A0 hands its spawner (0x080D7B54) AttackVars +0x28, a pointer to his own object's +0x68 (written at 0x080F9F64), in r3, which the third kind's spawner stores as Z (+0x3C) and the box keeps at +0x60; its init (0x080D78F2) clears Z's upper half: Z's lower half the pointer's, his object's place in each game's T1 table (numberman_v1 at t157: BN5 0xB340, BN6 0xAAF0)

spawn_leftovers.why: A word of an object of a moved type that the third kind's spawner takes from a register its caller never set (BN5's spawn keeps r1-r3 as +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C and r4 as +4, 0x080030DC-0x080030E6; BN6's the same): each game's engine leaves its own value there as it runs the Navi's state, BN5's its AI data's address, BN6's a small number. Neither the object's code nor the engine's routines it runs read the word, so the two are the same object: read as the rule names them, BN5's an AI data's start and BN6's the number `bn6`, and nothing else let through.

rules.evidence: BlizzardMan's slide's hit (the third kind's 0x2F, moved): his state at BN5 0x080FE646-0x080FE68C hands its spawner (0x080CA8FE: push {r0-r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x2F; bl 0x08003178) r3 untouched since his state began (0x0800D1C6 and 0x0800C6CA, called between, keep it), so its +0x3C is what each game's state dispatch left in r3 (BN5's 0x08017BD0 by 0x080F2348, BN6's 0x0801AF44 by 0x080F36A4): BN5's his AI data, BN6's 3 (blizzardman_v1 at t784). Its routines (0x080CA838-0x080CA91C) read and write no +0x3C-0x3F, nor do the engine's it calls (0x0800C69C, 0x08016126, 0x0800325C, 0x08016760, 0x08016C34, 0x08016B1A, 0x080167B0, 0x08016C04, 0x08008B6E, 0x08008A78, 0x0800C6CA, 0x0800B334, 0x08016B60, 0x08016B88, 0x080138EA, walked four calls deep); it draws no sprite.

CosmoMan's (the third kind's 0x79, moved): its spawner (0x080D56E0: push {r0,r1,r5}; movs r0,#0x79; bl 0x08003178; then strb r2,[r0,#4], its count of frames) is called from his routine 0x080FF9C0 (at 0x080FF9F4), which sets no r4 and calls only routines that keep it (0x080014A6, 0x0800DBAE, 0x08016C56), so the spawn's +4 word is what each game's state dispatch left in r4, a place in MegaMan's AI data (BN5's +0x74 region, BN6's +0x84: cosmoman_v1 at t39), its low byte then the count. Its routine (0x080D5634-0x080D56CC) reads and writes +4 alone, a byte (ldrb, subs, strb at 0x080D568C-0x080D5690), and no +5-+7; the engine's it calls (0x08016126, 0x0800325C, 0x08016760, 0x08016B90, 0x08016B1A, 0x080167B0, 0x08008B6E, 0x08016B88, walked four calls deep) read +4 and +5 only of its collision data (0x080167B4, 0x08016642), never of the object; it draws no sprite. The low byte is compared (compares: byte 0), the upper three are each engine's leftover.

CosmoMan's (the third kind's 0x6C, moved): his routine at BN5 0x080FFE30-0x080FFE86 hands its spawner (0x080D3828: push {r0-r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x6C; bl 0x08003178) an r3 it never sets, the last writer an engine routine it calls (0x080090E8 at 0x080FFE44, or 0x08016C56 at 0x080FFE54; then 0x0800C6CA, his own 0x081002E0 and 0x0800C676, none writing r3), so the spawn's Z (+0x3C) is that leftover; the spawner then writes Z's upper half itself (movs r2,#0x10; strh r2,[r0,#0x3E]), 16 in both, and its low half stays each engine's (BN5 0x41D0, BN6 3: cosmoman_v1 at t438). Its code (0x080D3648-0x080D3962, its states 0x080D366C, 0x080D36EA and 0x080D3820 from its table 0x080D3660) reads no +0x3C-0x3F, and the engine's it calls read Z only at 0x0800C6B4 (0x0800C6AC: its place from X, Y and Z, whose panel routine 0x0800C658 reads X and Y alone, r2 unread), walked four calls deep. Z's upper half (bytes 2 and 3, the height a draw takes) is compared; its low half is each engine's leftover.

SearchMan's (the fourth kind's 0x5A, moved): his state at BN5 0x080F5748-0x080F5752 loads r3 with his AI data's +0x2C (ldr r3,[r7,#0x2C], an object's address in each game's RAM) to read its row and column (+0x12, +0x13), then calls the 0x5A's spawner (0x080E7020: push {r0-r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x5A; bl 0x080031CC), the fourth kind's spawner, the third's (0x08003178) with kind 4: r1-r3 kept as +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C. So the 0x5A's Z (+0x3C) is that address; its init (0x080E6FA8) writes its upper half 0x10 (strh r0,[r5,#0x3E] at 0x080E6FB0) and its code counts it down (0x080E6FB4-0x080E6FB8), reading no +0x3C or its low half (its states 0x080E6FA9, 0x080E6FF9 from its table 0x080E6F98; the engine's routines it runs draw by Z's upper half). Its low half is each game's address's: seen in bn5_searchman_v1, _v1_keys and _sp at the 0x5A's first frame, BN5 0xB200, BN6 0xA9B0, its upper half 0x10 in both.

CosmoMan's (the third kind's 0x6D, moved): its spawner (0x080D3964, spawned by the 0x6C) copies its parent's X, Y and Z (ldr r1,[r5,#0x3C]; str r1,[r0,#0x3C] at 0x080D397C-0x080D397E), so its Z is the 0x6C's, each engine's leftover in its low half as the 0x6C's rule above says. Its code (0x080D3898-0x080D3962, its states 0x080D38BC, 0x080D38F6 and 0x080D395C from its table 0x080D38B0) reads no +0x3C-0x3F, the engine's it calls only 0x0800C6AC's, as the 0x6C's (cosmoman_v1 at t438). Z's upper half is compared; its low half is each engine's leftover.

rng.why: rng=replay (src/dev/xdiff_events.c): each of BN6's draws is keyed by the family's own code that led to it (its BN5 address, through what the install moved) or else by its caller, a BN6 routine's place read as the same place in its BN5 twin (twins), and the k-th draw of a key in a frame (by the battle's timer before it) is given the word the reference's k-th of that key drew from, written into the RNG word it reads, before it reads it: the family's code draws BN5's numbers whatever the engine drew around it. A draw of either game with no twin in the other's frame is reported, never forced: the engine's own draws one game alone makes (only) are explained there, each with both games' routines; any other is a difference (the family's where its code led to it).

masks.name: the renderer's slots
masks.why: Each frame the sprite renderer gives each object drawn a place for its tiles in OBJ VRAM (its sprite state's +0x08, u16) from a running count over all it draws before it, and keeps the frame it last copied there (+0x24), cleared when the place moves. The code is the same in both, but what each game draws (MegaMan's own sprite, the HUD, BN6's own effects) differs, so the places do. Drawing resources, not anyone's logic: an object's animation is compared by its sprite state's animation (+0x00) and the pointers to its current frame (+0x1C, +0x20, relative to its sprite's data). This mask is for what is not the family's (MegaMan's side, a native's, the engine's); the family's places are read as their rank among the family's own (maps, renderer) and its cache (+0x24) is compared. The lava's spark (whose panels: the code under test, as a family's), the spark the family's attack strikes with (whose spark) and an effect the engine's code gives for it (whose effect) likewise: its place there is the count of what was drawn before it, MegaMan's own sprite among it.
evidence: the tile place: BN5 0x081C7FF4-0x081C7FFC / BN6 0x081D658C-0x081D6594 (the IWRAM renderer's ROM copies), the frame copied to 0x06010000 + place x 32 (BN5 0x081C800E / BN6 0x081D65A6), its cache cleared where the place moved (BN5 0x081C7FD4 / BN6 0x081D656C)
a sprite's data pointer +0x18 is its data's start + 4 (the sprite's set-up stores it so), so +0x1C-0x24 are compared from it

masks.name: BN6's state saved as he leaves a form
masks.why: As MegaMan is asked to leave a form (his AI data +0x44 bit 0x40), BN6's player update clears his object's +0x5C and saves his state word (+8) there before the change's action (0x1C); BN5's twin asks the same change (0x1A) and saves nothing. The word stays after the change in BN6, unread by the rest of his battle (a Cross's end the same). The engine's, not the Soul's.
evidence: BN6 0x08017C40-0x08017C4C (in 0x08017BC0): str 0 to +0x5C, then +8's word stored there where it reads 0; BN5 0x0801467A-0x08014686 (in its twin 0x08014604): the request's bit cleared, 0x100 set, setAttack0(0x1A), nothing more
soul_knight: BN6's +0x5C 0x00040804 from t1564, the turn his Soul ended, BN5's 0

masks.name: the engine's draws while the battle's clock holds
masks.why: Both games draw three random numbers each frame whatever the battle does (rng, per_frame: the game state's GetRNG and GetRNGSecondary, the main loop's GetRNGSecondary), the battle's clock (its timer) still or not. Where it holds for a number of frames each game's own, each game's words step as many times more as it had frames more, and the first traced frame after shows them apart; rng=follow writes BN6's from BN5's after it. Two holds differ: a turn's change opened with L takes BN6 four frames more than BN5 (three as it begins: BN6 runs its turn's form check before its Custom screen, 0x0800840C calling 0x0801483C, which BN5 skips in a battle not linked, 0x0800773C through 0x0802D510; one more as the turn starts after it, 52 frames against 53); and a Soul's unison is BN5's own crossing, longer than the proxy's (the summon behind it HeatMan's, src/emu/soulproxy.c) by 6 frames, until the Souls track's S3 brings BN5's image. The engine's, not the Soul's: held only where every other draw since the last traced frame is the same in number in both and each word is the other's stepped by exactly the per-frame draws one game made more.
evidence: soul_knight, the frames of each hold (src/dev/xdiff.c's trace and the cores' frames): at t523 BN5 2 frames of the fight's phase then 52 of the Custom screen's closed window, BN6 5 and 53 (the Custom screen itself the same, 37 frames); at t0 BN5 194 frames, BN6 188 (the unison against the proxy's crossing)

BN6 0x0800840C (the turn's step before the Custom screen): the packets copied (0x080147E4), the form check (0x0801483C: a pending form or Beast Out's end, 0x0801486C), Beast Out's counter (0x08015A38); BN5 0x0800773C: bl 0x0802D510, bne past its check, in a battle that is not linked

masks.name: BN6's hit flag by a chip's icon element
masks.why: As a chip is used BN6's engine ORs into its attack element (MegaMan's AttackVars +2, his AI data +0xA2) a hit flag by its record's icon element (Sword 0x80, Cursor 0x40, Wind 0x20, Break 0x10: the table at 0x080129E4), which BN6's hit pass acts on (a Break breaks a guard, a Sword is a sword); BN5's chip use writes the element alone. BN6's engine rule for every chip, BN5's among them (docs/multirom/one-net.md: the chips' finer calls); the flag is the one the chip in use (his AttackVars +0x14) has by its icon element, BN6's record's or, for a chip of the registry's own, its BN5 record's as BN6's (src/core/xchips_record.c).
evidence: BN6 0x0801271E-0x08012728 (the chip's numbers written for its attack, 0x080126E4): ldrb r1,[r6,#4]; ldrb r2,[r6,#6]; ldr r0,=0x080129E4; ldrb r0,[r0,r2]; orrs r1,r0; strb r1,[r7,#2]
BN5 0x0800FEA4-0x0800FEA6 (its twin, 0x0800FE6A): ldrb r1,[r6,#4]; strb r1,[r7,#2]
the table's 16 bytes: 00 00 00 00 00 80 40 00 20 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 (icon element 5 Sword, 6 Cursor, 8 Wind, 9 Break)
chip_sword: MegaMan's +0xA2 0 in BN5's and 0x80 in BN6's from the Sword's use (t32) on

masks.name: the sword's slash's last frame
masks.why: A sword's slash is an effect object (the fourth kind's type 0, effect 0x18: sprite list 3's 0x14, its animation 2, both games' effect tables alike; a Katana's 0x16 and 0x17 its animations 0 and 1), drawn from each game's own sprite: BN5's animation 2 has four frames (4, 3, 3 and 2 frames), BN6's three (4, 3, 3), so BN5's slash is still drawn (its frame's place on) the frame BN6's ends, and lives two frames longer. Its place and first frames are compared.
evidence: the effects' tables: BN5 0x080DFD7C + 0x18 x 4, BN6 0x080E16D4 + 0x18 x 4: 0C 14 02 00 in both
the sprites: BN5 0x0830105C, BN6 0x0830E6BC (list 3's 0x14), their animation 2's frames 4, 3, 3, 2 and 4, 3, 3
chip_sword: the slash in play from t44 in both, to t54 in BN6's and t56 in BN5's, its flags and frame apart at t54
chip_katana1: Katana's second slash (effect 0x16, list 3's 0x14's animation 0, both tables 0C 14 00 00) ended in BN6's at t57 while BN5's is still drawn

masks.name: the spark effect's last frames
masks.why: Effect 0x11 (the fourth kind's type 0) draws the hit spark's sprite, list 5's 5, its animation 1 (both games' effect tables alike), each game its own sprite: BN5's animation 1 has five frames of 2, BN6's four, so BN5's effect is still drawn (in play, its state 4) the two frames after BN6's ends (its state 8, then gone), as the hit spark's own life ('the hit spark's life'). Its place and first frames are compared.
evidence: the effects' tables: BN5 0x080DFD7C + 0x11 x 4, BN6 0x080E16D4 + 0x11 x 4: 14 05 01 00 in both
the sprites: BN5 0x0837D994, BN6 0x083A0320 (list 5's 5), their animation 1's frames 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 and 2, 2, 2, 2
chip_cannball: CannBall's burst (effect 0x11, from its moved code) ended in BN6's at t100 (its state 8) while BN5's is still drawn

masks.name: BN6's support family's extra frame
masks.why: BN6's support family (0x15, 0x080ED0DC) runs the chip's routine, marks its AttackVars +1 and ends the attack at its next frame (0x080ED130: object_exitAttackState), where BN5's (0x080EC400) ends it in the frame it runs the routine (0x080EC448): MegaMan stands in CurAction 0x15 a frame longer in BN6's engine and goes through his after-chip wait (his +0x20 counted down from 9, his +0x0A/+0x0B, his AI data +0x48) a frame behind BN5's, the same values a frame later. BN6's engine's own family for every support chip, BN5's included (docs/multirom/one-net.md: the chips' finer calls); each such byte must be the one BN5's MegaMan had the frame before.
evidence: BN6 0x080ED0DC-0x080ED134: phase 0 runs the routine (0x080ED102) and sets AttackVars +1 (0x080ED12C); phase 1 ends the attack (0x080ED130)
BN5 0x080EC400-0x080EC44C: runs the routine (0x080EC420), then ends the attack (0x080EC448), one phase
chip_areagrab: MegaMan's CurAction 0x15 at t32 in both, his ready state's from t33 in BN5's and t34 in BN6's, every byte of it a frame behind until t44

masks.name: WideSht's wave's spawn word
masks.why: BN6's WideSht family (0x30) hands its wave's spawner r3 = 0x100000 where BN5's (0x25) hands 0, and the common spawn keeps the caller's r1-r4 as the object's words (r3 at +0x3C): the wave's +0x3E reads 0x10 in BN6's battle alone. No code of the wave's reads its +0x3C (its routines, BN5 0x080CC878 / BN6 0x080CCD0C, walked), and the battle goes on the same.
evidence: BN5 0x080ED132: movs r3,#0, then bl 0x080CCA62 (the wave's spawner); BN6 0x080EE93C-0x080EE93E: movs r3,#0x10; lsls r3,r3,#0x10, then bl 0x080CCEF6
the common spawn BN6 0x080032BC-0x080032C6: ldm r7!,{r0-r4} (the caller's r0-r4, pushed by its spawner); strb r0,[r5,#1]; str r1,[r5,#0x34]; str r2,[r5,#0x38]; str r3,[r5,#0x3c]; str r4,[r5,#4]
chip_widesht1-3: the wave's +0x3E 0 in BN5's and 0x10 in BN6's from its spawn, every other byte of it the same

masks.name: BN6's spread shot's region
masks.why: The spread shot (the third kind's type 0x12, Spreader's) sets up its collision with region 61 for what it is in BN6 (0x080C8202: movs r1,#0x3d) where BN5's sets region 0 (0x080C6CCE: movs r1,#0): BN6's table gives region 61 the word 0x80 (BN6's bit by which its second pass lets an object whose +0x3C has 0x20 touch it, 0x081D7BAE), BN5's region 0 none. evidence: BN5 0x080C6CCE-0x080C6CD4 / BN6 0x080C8202-0x080C8208: the shot's collision setup (BN5 0x08016760 / BN6 0x08019FB4) with r1 0 / 0x3D, r2 5
the alliance tables at region 61 (entries 122, 123): BN5 0x80000080, 0x40000080; BN6 0x80, 0x80; at region 0 both 0

masks.name: BN6's hit flag on a chip's objects
masks.why: The hit flag BN6's chip use ORs into the chip's attack element by its icon element (the mask above) goes on with the element: the chip's objects take it as their element (+0x0E, from the family's r2), and BN6's collision setup keeps the element's high nibble apart at its +0x19 (0x08019FC4-0x08019FC8: ands #0xF0; strb [r7,#0x19]), a place BN5's layout has none of. An object of the fourth kind a support routine spawns keeps r2, the element, at +0x38 (the common spawn's words: r1-r4 at +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C, +4).
evidence: BN6's collision setup 0x08019FBA-0x08019FC8: the object's +0x0E, its low nibble to +2 and its high to +0x19
chip_airhoc: the puck's +0x0E and its collision data's +0x19 0x10 (Break, AirHoc's icon element) in BN6's battle alone, from its spawn (t35)
chip_nrthwind: NrthWind's wind (the fourth kind's type 0x39) +0x38 0x20 (Wind, its icon element) in BN6's battle alone

masks.why: After the puck BN5's AirHoc (its family 0x21) and BN6's AirHocky (0x26, whose code the registry's AirHoc plays) wait 15 frames before the attack ends, at the same frame: BN6's sets its timer (AttackVars +0x10, 15) as its first phase ends (0x080EE05E) where BN5's sets it at its second phase's start with that phase's mark (AttackVars +1, 4: 0x080ECE18-0x080ECE1E): for one frame BN6's timer reads 15 where BN5's still 0, and through the wait BN5's +1 reads 4 where BN6's 0.
