BN6 0x080EE056-0x080EE064 (phase 0's end: +0x10 15, strh 4 to +0); its phase 1 counts it down
chip_airhoc: AttackVars +0x10 15 at t47 in BN6's, 14 at t48 in both, the attack's end at t63 in both

masks.name: BN6's hurt sound on a lethal hit
masks.why: A hit that takes its object's HP to 0: BN6's damage routine plays the hurt sound (0x6B MegaMan's, 0x6D another's) before it tests the HP left, BN5's skips it on a lethal hit (its test first): the engine's damage step, not the family's code, a song in BN6's frame alone, those two alone (the deletion that follows is compared).
evidence: BN6 0x0801BA3C: bl 0x0800E2D8; push {r1}; movs r4,#0x6D ... movs r4,#0x6B; bl 0x080005CC; pop {r1}; tst r1,r1
BN5 0x080185C4: bl 0x0800C6D8; tst r1,r1; beq 0x080185FE, past its sound 0x080185D0-0x080185E8
zomon_v3 at t1084 and zomon_v3ex at t760: MegaMan's HP 0 in both at t1083 and t759, song 0x6B in BN6's frame alone, its event's caller the engine's (0x0801BA5F)

bn4.about: What may differ between BN4 Red Sun's battle (the reference, tools/xdiff_bn4.py) and BN6's with a BN4 family moved in, and why: each allowed difference scoped to whose records it is and the fields it moves, its evidence both games' code by address; never a blanket mask

allowed.name: BN6's battle a fight frame behind BN4's
allowed.fields: every record of BN6's battle, the same offset for all (tools/xdiff_bn4.py compare: the family's, MegaMan's and the world's objects, their AI and collision data, the panels, the run order, the sounds, the events and the family's draws), BN6's at t + 1 against BN4's at t; BN6's battle traced a fight frame longer and its keys by the timer taken a frame later (src/dev/xdiff.c, Side.behind), the family's own draws given BN4's of the frame before (rng=replay with lag=1, src/dev/xdiff_events.h xd_replay_lag). Every record a state drives, that is: what the battle's timer drives is compared at the same fight frame, its clock shown by its writer (bn4.clocks, bn4.sounds' clock). What still differs under the shift fails the spec (the family's) or keeps it INCONCLUSIVE (the world's), never a field or a role given a lag of its own; what is fixed before the first state keeps its own handling (BN6's per-frame RNG steps, not compared where the draws are replayed; BN6's MegaMan's companion, spawned by his init)
allowed.why: BN6's engine runs no state while the opening is paused, BN4's does, so BN6's whole battle runs a fight frame behind BN4's from the first state on. Both games' pause byte (BN4's [eToolkit+0x40]+9, BN6's [eToolkit+0x3C]+0xA) reads 1 from the appear to the fight, and each object runner (BN4 0x0800314C, BN6 0x080031AC) runs a paused object whose +0 has 0x04. BN4's state runner (0x08013C48) has no pause test and calls the state (0x08013D9A), so in the opening BN4's generic state 1 (0x0801013A) hands a virus its first own state and MegaMan's state 1 (0x08010A88) his ready 6, each run at the fight's first frame. BN6's (0x0801B1C4, from the virus dispatcher 0x0810A29C and MegaMan's update) tests the pause byte first (0x0800A03C, at 0x0801B1CC) and, for a CurAction not 0 whose flags (0x0801A166) have none of 0x40000100 and whose struck word (0x0801A180) has no 0x8000, returns at 0x0801B21A (b 0x0801B37A) without calling the state: BN6's state 1 (a virus's 0x080165B8, MegaMan's 0x08017888) runs at the fight's first frame and the first own state at the second (billy_v1: Billy's first own state at t1 in BN4 and t2 in BN6; MegaMan's ready setting his object's +0xB 4 and +0x20 9 at t1 in BN4, t2 in BN6, the same count-down to t10 and t11). Everything the states do follows a frame later: Billy's moves and reservations, its thunder striking MegaMan (t431 in BN4, t432 in BN6), the sounds they play. BN6's own Mettaur against BN4's starts the same way (game=bn4:bn6, foes=01@52). The lead's call (2026-11-04, the owner's to overturn): one offset for the whole battle, where the owner's earlier call (the port keeps BN6's timing) had it for the family alone. BN6's first fight frame, its states' 1, meets BN4's paused opening, which the trace does not keep, and is not compared

allowed.name: the family's object +0 bit 0x04, which BN6's generic state 1 keeps
allowed.why: The bit the object runner runs a paused object by (BN4 0x0800314C at 0x08003174, BN6 0x080031AC at 0x080031D8: tst r4,#4 while the pause byte is set), set on every first-kind object as it spawns (both games' kind 1 descriptors' flags byte 0x19, BN4 0x08003268, BN6 0x080032D0, then 0x17 once it appears). BN4's generic state 1 clears it (0x0801013A: ldrb r0,[r5]; movs r1,#4; bics r0,r1; strb r0,[r5]), as it hands a virus its first own state during the paused opening, so the virus waits for the fight; BN6's (0x080165B8) does not, BN6's state runner never running a state while paused (0x0801B21A, the family's timeline above). The same engine difference as the lag: BN6's own Mettaur keeps 0x04 too (0x17 at t1 against BN4's Mettaur's 0x13, game=bn4:bn6, foes=01@52)

allowed.name: the struck's push's kind, BN6's own byte
allowed.why: BN6 keeps the kind of a step an object takes at its +0x0F (the entry "BN6's MegaMan's step's kind", the same byte): its struck pass of the first kind stores 1 there as it gives a hit's push (0x0801AC2C-0x0801AC2E with the struck-and-pushed status 0x100, 0x0801AC42-0x0801AC44 with the push alone's 0x10; BN6_STEP_BEGIN's four more stores alike), and its slide's step reads it as the row of its table (0x0800E468: ldrb r0,[r5,#0xf] at 0x0800E46C, into 0x0800E498's table at 0x0800E4AC). BN4's pass sets the statuses alone (0x08013618-0x08013622, 0x08013632-0x08013634) and no byte of the object's, its slide's step (0x0800ACAA) taking its row from the collision data's push bits (+0xD, 0x0800ACB2). BN4's +0x0F is its enemy id's byte, read as BN6's NameID by the trace, so BN4's side holds 0 there. A family's object struck and pushed keeps BN6's 1 from the hit on (bn4_chip_mokorus1's Mettaur from t93 to the trace's end: its struck state is the family's own, which never runs BN6's pushed state's end, 0x08016804-0x08016806, where BN6 clears it). The push itself, the struck's panels, states and timers, is compared as ever: that Mettaur pushed from (5,2) to (6,2) two frames after the hit in both, its state 5 from the hit's frame

allowed.name: the rock's debris, each engine's own art
allowed.why: A falling rock's debris (GutsMan's rocks, BN4's third-kind 0x1D, moved: their code at BN4 0x080D09E8 spawns four on landing) is each engine's own fourth-kind 0x09, spawned by twin spawners (BN4 0x080E29F8, BN6 0x080E23C0: the same bytes but the spawn's bl, the symbol map's pair; its +0x40 and +0x48 the speeds of BN4's table 0x080D0A20, copied with the rock's code), its init the same instructions but for its sprite's number (BN4 0x080E2934, its jump table 0x080E2924; BN6 0x080E22FC): sprite_load of list 0x10 (4) with number 0x0E in BN4 (0x080E2942, its bl to 0x0800287C), BN4's rocks' own sprite, which GutsMan's recipe copies as list 4 0xCA for his rocks, and number 5 in BN6 (0x080E230A, its bl to 0x080026E4), BN6's own rock art (0x08353D1C). Its sprite state (+0x80 to +0xBB: its frames' pointers into its art, the frame's count and flags read from it) is its art's: gutsman_v1's at t361 (BN4) and t362 (BN6), the hooks' sprite events from 0x080E2949 and 0x080E2311. Its place, speeds, spawn, life and every other byte compared as ever

allowed.name: the thunder's sprite, BN6's own art
allowed.why: Billy's thunder is BN6's own third-kind 0x2A run for Billy's parameters (the recipe's audit, tools/bn4_twins.py AUDITS (0x080D2156, 0x080CADBC): BN6's object, not BN4's moved), so it draws BN6's own art: its init sets up sprite list 0x10, number 0x11 in BN4 (0x080D2044, its sprite_load 0x0800287C) and number 0x16 in BN6 (0x080CAC80, sprite_load 0x080026E4), two sprites of other bytes (the hooks' CRC32s 0x030B3B0A and 0xAF2AFC99). What the sprite state holds of it is its own: +0xA8 to +0xB7 its frames' pointers into it (sprite_load's +0x18 on, its state at the object's +0x90) and +0xB8's word (its top byte 0x80 in BN4, 0xC0 in BN6) copied from the sprite's own data (BN6 0x0800210E-0x08002120, byte by byte as the art has it): Billy's sprite, a copy of BN4's bytes, holds the same there in both games (+0xBB 0xFC), MegaMan's too (0xF0). The thunder's place, timing, damage and hit are compared as ever

allowed.name: MegaMan's attack's entry, BN6's own number
allowed.why: BN6's setAttack has six entries (0x08011680 to 0x08011694, each movs r2,#n for n 0 to 5) that fall into one body (0x08011698), which sets the object's CurAction and phase word, zeroes the attack variables' first halfword and stores the entry's number at their +0x1C (strb r2,[r1,#0x1c] at 0x080116A6, r1 the AI data + 0xA0: AI data +0xBC). BN4's is one entry (0x0800C9AC: the same stores at the object's +9 and +0xA and the variables' first halfword, its AI data + 0x70, then mov pc,lr) and keeps no number. A chip's attack is BN6's entry 2 (0x08011688): 2 in BN6 from t33 as Cannon begins, 0 in BN4 (bn4_chip_cannon; the other 35 bytes of the variables the same in both through the chip). BN6's own; where BN4's byte there held anything it is compared as ever.

allowed.name: MegaMan's chips held, BN6's own count
allowed.why: BN6 counts the chips its MegaMan holds in his object's +0x1A (bn6f's ChipsHeld): set as the hand is given him (the store at 0x0800FE0C, in the routine at 0x0800FDEA, with the next chip at +0x2A) and one less as a chip is used (0x0800F322 to 0x0800F32A); two more routines write it (0x080165F8, 0x08016EE0). None of the four is located in BN4 by its bytes (tools/bn6f_match.py's map of bn6f's functions in BN4), and BN4's MegaMan's +0x1A reads 0 through a battle in which he holds and uses a chip (bn4_chip_cannon's trace: 1 in BN6 from the first frame, 0 from t33 as Cannon is used, 0 in BN4 throughout): BN4 keeps its hand's count elsewhere. BN6's own; where BN4's byte there held anything it is compared as ever.

allowed.name: MegaMan's own sprite
allowed.why: MegaMan is drawn from each game's own art: his sprite state's frame pointers (+0xA8 to +0xB7, sprite_load's +0x18 on, his state at +0x90) point into BN4's sprite list 0's entry 0 (0x08214000, BN4's lists 0x0802793C) and BN6's own MegaMan (0x081D8000, as BN5's differential has it: legit.json's masks, MegaMan's own sprite), and +0xB8's word is copied from that art's data (BN6 0x0800210E-0x08002120): his place, his CurAction and what he does are compared as ever

allowed.name: MegaMan's own art's animation
allowed.fields: his sprite's count (+0x91) and its last frame's bit (+0x92's 0x80), only where each game's are what its own art gives at the same place of the same animation: the animation (+0x90) the same, and the frames run of it the same in both, each read from its own game's art by his frame's record (+0xAC) and his count (tools/xdiff_bn4.py own_animation, anim_place); his animation and its place compared as ever, so a state that starts it a frame apart, or an animation run longer or shorter, still parts
allowed.why: His art is each game's own ("MegaMan's own sprite": BN4's sprite list 0's entry 0, 0x08214000; BN6's 0x081D8000), and each cuts an animation into its own frames: a frame's record is 20 bytes, its duration at +16 and +18's 0x80 its last (tools/xsoul.py anim_life's reading), and the sprite update (BN4 0x0800285C, BN6 0x080026C4) loads a frame's duration less 1 into the count and counts it down a frame each fight frame, the next frame's record (+0xAC) at 0, +0x92's 0x80 set as the last begins. His struck animation (1, set by his state 3 at the hit: walla_v1, t68) runs 24 frames in both, as 4,2,2,2,2,2,4,4,2 in BN4's art and 4,2,2,2,2,4,5,3 in BN6's (both ROMs read by the anim_place walk), so from its sixth frame (t80) the count reads otherwise (BN4's 1, BN6's 3) and BN6's last frame begins a frame sooner (t89, BN4's t90) at the same frames run, and his state ends it at t91 in both. Each game's sprite art, not the port's subject

allowed.name: MegaMan's object +0 bit 0x04, which BN6's state 1 of his keeps
allowed.why: As a virus's (the family's entry above): BN4's MegaMan's state 1 (0x08010A88, his state table 0x080EAEFC, run by his update 0x080EAECC from his type's 0x080B34D8) clears his +0 0x04 (ldrb r0,[r5]; movs r1,#4; bics; strb at 0x08010A8A-0x08010A90) as it sets his ready 6; BN6's (0x08017888, his state table 0x080EB86C by his AI data's +1, from his mode 2's routine 0x080EB7A0) sets his ready 8 and keeps it (0x080178AC-0x080178B2), BN6's state runner never running a state while paused (0x0801B21A): the bit the object runner runs a paused object by, BN6's set and BN4's not; his CurAction is compared as ever

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's routine index
allowed.why: BN6's MegaMan runs as the first kind's type 0, whose routine picks his by his AI data +0 (0x080B9A5C: ldr r4,[r5,#0x58]; ldrb r0,[r4]; the table at 0x080B9A74: 0 the virus dispatcher 0x0810A279, 2 his own 0x080EB7A1, his +0 2); BN4's MegaMan's type routine calls his own straight (0x080B34D8: bl 0x080EAEA8) and reads no such index; BN4's AI data +0 is his third power attack (0x0800C9E8), read as BN6's +8

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's fourth power attack
allowed.why: BN6's attack state calls four power-attack dispatchers (0x080F17CA +6, 0x080F17F2 +7, 0x080F182E +8, 0x080F185A +4: 0x0801177A), BN4's three (0x080EEC1E +0xD, 0x080EEC3E +0xF, 0x080EEC5E +0, then on as BN6's after its fourth: BN4 bl 0x0800B72C; cmp r0,r3, BN6 bl 0x0800FB54; cmp r0,r3): BN6's +4, set by its loadout (0x080144C0, 0xFF none), has no BN4 twin

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's companion
allowed.why: BN6's player init spawns a fourth-kind 0x08 for MegaMan and keeps it at his AI data +0x58 (0x080173CA-0x080173CE: r7 his AI data + 0x58, bl 0x080E223E: movs r0,#8; the fourth kind's spawn; its +0x4C him; str r0,[r7]); BN4's twin of that spawner (0x080E28EC: movs r0,#8, the same spawn and owner, no AI data store) has no BL calling it, and BN4's MegaMan's AI data +0x58 stays 0: the object, its place in the run order and the pointer to it are BN6's alone

allowed.name: BN4's MegaMan's loadout's unread first byte
allowed.why: BN4's loadout setter (0x0800BD48, from the form's state 0x0800E05C) writes his AI data +0xC as the loadout's first byte: 0xFF for form 0 (0x0800BD74) or the form's loadout word (0x0800BD5E, 0x080184F0, whose +0 is 0xFF in every form); no code of BN4's reads it through an AI data pointer (every load at +0xC whose base came from an object's +0x58 in the ROM's first 2 MB: none). BN6's loadout (0x080144C0) keeps no such byte, its +0xC no field of his; BN4's power attacks his loadout does keep are mapped (+0xD, +0xE, +0xF, +0 at BN6's +6, +5, +7, +8, xdiff_bn4_trace.c)

allowed.name: BN4's MegaMan's charge times, cached
allowed.why: BN4 caches the charge times of his chip charge's and charged shot's power attacks (AI data +0xE and +0xF) as his loadout is set (0x0800BCF4: BN4_CHARGE_TIMES by power attack and his Charge, NaviStats +7; 0xFF none) into u16 +0x34 and +0x36, and its charge levels compare his two charge counters with them (0x0800BB56, 0x0800BB6C). BN6 caches none: its twin reads the same kind of table at each test (0x08012F62: r7 5 for A, 7 for B, 0x11 a Beast chip; BN6_CHARGE_TIMES read at 0x08012FA6 by his Charge, 0x08013774), the trace keeps BN4's cache in the spare's last word (BN6_AI_SPARE_LAST, xdiff_bn4_trace.c), BN6's +0x34 being his anger, BN4's +0x2E (BN4_AI_ANGER); the power attacks themselves are compared (mapped)

allowed.name: BN4's MegaMan's control block's pointer
allowed.why: BN4's AI data's clear (0x0800B7CE) points each side's +0x50 at its control block (side 0's 0x02035A70, side 1's 0x02035AB0, 0x40 bytes each, cleared by 0x0800E8FE), which his ready routine (0x080EED48) sets up (+0: 0x0800EB86 tests it; 0x0800EAC6 then fills its 0x40 bytes, 0x0800EB8E sets +0) and runs his ready's sub-state from (+1: 0x0800E4F8's table). BN6's ready (0x080F1694, by his object's +0xA) keeps no such block and no pointer: his AI data +0x50 is 0. The ready's phases both games keep in his object (+0xA, +0xB, +0x20) are compared as ever

allowed.name: BN6's AI data's pool bit
allowed.why: BN6 hands its actors' AI data from a pool of eight (BN6_AI_POOL): the take (0x0800ED2C) sets the entry's own bit into its +0x7C (MegaMan's entry 0, bit 31: +0x7F 0x80), which the let-go (0x0800ED80) reads to free it. BN4 keeps one AI data a side at a fixed place (0x0800BFF4: movs r1,#0xc0; muls, from BN4_AI_DATA) and no pool, so no such bit (its +0x7C one of its attack's variables, at BN6's +0xAC in the trace)

allowed.name: BN6's AI data's palette step
allowed.why: BN6's battle actors' setup (0x0800768C) writes the enemy record 1's +2 into the AI data's +3 (MegaMan's 1); it is read only by the actor init's palette (0x0800F334, its one caller 0x08016F90 in the virus and Navi init 0x08016F56, not his player init 0x080172F0: palette = 0x0800F354[version] x step) and by a virus's version change (0x0810A90A), neither run for MegaMan. BN4's viruses keep no AI data and its MegaMan's has no such step; BN4's own +3, the HP bug's count (0x0800C164), is BN6's +9 (0x08010230), mapped

allowed.name: BN6's AI data's unused HP mark
allowed.why: BN6's AI data +0xE reads 0xFF from its setup; its two readers keep nothing of it: 0x0800A86E walks the eight alive actors and loads the HP of one whose +0xE is not 0xFF, then returns without using it, and the common delete state 0x08016C4E (MegaMan's too, his routine's table 0x080EB7B8) loads his HP into r1 and drops it as it writes 0xFF there (0x08016C66-0x08016C70). BN4 has no such mark (its +0xE the chip charge's power attack, BN6's +5, mapped)

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's Beast Out gate
allowed.why: BN6's battle start writes 1 into both sides' players' AI data +0xF (0x08009338: 0x0800936E, 0x0800937E); it is read only by Beast Out's: its end (0x080159C6, BN6_TURN_END's call: 0 there sets 2, then the Beast Out counter, NaviStats +0x29) and its count-down (0x08015A16 for both sides, while NaviStats +0x29 is 0: one less to 0, 0xFF left). BN4 has no Beast Out, and no byte of its MegaMan's AI data its code reads so

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's Beast chip charge
allowed.why: BN6's loadout (0x080144C0) writes +0x11 0xFF, the power attack its chip charge takes for a chip whose record +6 is 0xA in place of +5's (the chip charge's dispatcher 0x0800FB54 at 0x0800FB96, the charge time 0x08012F62 at 0x08012F8E: r7 0x11). BN4's chip charge (0x0800B72C, its flag 8) branches by his form alone (0x0800B770: form 5 0x0800D638, else 0x0800D4B4) and caches only +0xE's and +0xF's charge times (0x0800BCF4): no byte like it

allowed.name: MegaMan's held chip, which neither battle reads of his
allowed.why: His object's u16 +0x2A, the chip an object uses next (0xFFFF none). Its writers: BN6's state of his at 0x0801741C (its table word 0x0801740C) stores 0xFFFF at 0x08017438 in the opening; BN4's state 2 (0x08010890) stores 0xFFFF at 0x080108AA, run in no frame of these specs, so his reads 0 all battle (BN4's other stores 0x0801017A, 0x0801020A, 0x08010D82, 0x08013256, 0x08013268, 0x08015134). Its readers, searched in both ROMs (every ldr, ldrh or ldrb at #0x2a in the battle engines, BN4 0x08008000-0x08020000 and BN6 0x08008000-0x08020000, and in MegaMan's own code, BN4 0x080EA000-0x080F2000 and BN6 0x080EB000-0x080F3000; every ldrh [r5,#0x2a] in the first 2 MB attributed to its type): BN6's four, 0x0800EDC6, 0x0800EE1A, 0x0800EE8E and 0x0800EF2A (in 0x0800ED90, 0x0800EDD0, 0x0800EE26, 0x0800EF02), each read it only for an object whose name's class (0x0800F29C) is not 2, a MegaMan's chip read from his side's battle hand instead (0x08010018, 0x0802E070); BN4's one, 0x08014AFE (0x08014AE8), reads it of the objects in its list at 0x0203BE40, which 0x080167C0 fills for an enemy, called only from the enemies' types' inits (13 calls, 0x080B3550 to 0x080C4024, none in MegaMan's type 0 0x080B34D8 or his init 0x0801079C); the other loads at +0x2A in those spans are a collision data's, an AI data's or eToolkit's (BN4 0x0800F6FC, 0x08012C8C; BN6 0x0800E7AE, 0x08012E50), and the first 2 MB's ldrh [r5,#0x2a] in BN4 are the viruses' types' own (2, 5, 8, 0x13 and on). Nothing of either battle consumes MegaMan's, so the value each game left there is its own; where BN4's side ever holds one (a chip of his), it is compared as ever

allowed.name: the hit's spark, each engine's own
allowed.fields: the fourth kind's 0x04 alone: its sprite state (+0x80 to +0xBB), its end where one game's animation ends first (+0's 0x02 cleared and +8 its state 8, the update's twins' stores) and its being in play, and so its place in the run order, where one game's has ended and the other's not; its place, its spawn, its first frame and every other byte compared as ever (tools/xdiff_bn4.py spark_own)
allowed.why: A hit's spark is each engine's own effect, the same object of each: spawned by the hit's spark routine, twins (BN4 0x08012F44, BN6 from 0x0801A0D8: the striker's place moved by a draw, BN4 0x08014620 / BN6 0x0801BDDE, replayed from BN4's: legit.json's bn4 rng_twins) through twin spawners of the fourth kind's 0x04 (BN4 0x080E2140, BN6 0x080E1C00), its init setting up the same sprite list and number in each game's own art (the hooks' sprite events, BN4 from 0x080E20D0 and BN6 from 0x080E1B8C, b 0x1405 in both; other bytes, CRC32 0x70A851CA and 0x25A05EF3) and its update twins (BN4 0x080E2122, BN6 0x080E1BE2) ending it as its animation ends (the sprite's end bit 0x80: +0's 0x02 cleared, its state 8). So its sprite state (frames, their pointers into its art, +0x80 to +0xBB) and how long it lives are its art's: in billy_v1 BN6's lives 3 frames less (to t443 against BN4's t446, under the battle's offset). The thunder's sprite is allowed so too ("the thunder's sprite, BN6's own art"). The same object where a family's own code makes the hit's effect: Walla's ring (walla_v1-v3, the third kind's 0x3C, moved: BN4_T3_WALLA_RING) calls the engine's routine for the effect its hits make each frame (BN4 0x080D4BEA: bl 0x08012F44; its copy's veneer to BN6's twin 0x0801A0D4, tools/bn4_twins.py AUDITS: BN6's, the same steps in BN6's layout), which draws the place (0x08014620 / 0x0801BDDE, replayed) and spawns the spark through the twin spawners (BN4 0x080E2140, BN6 0x080E1C00; the spawn events' family Walla's, BN4's call at 0x080D4BEA and its copy's), so the spark is counted the family's (its spawn passed through the family's code) and is still each engine's own effect: its sprite state and life allowed so on the family's records too, that object alone (tools/xdiff_bn4.py compare), its spawn, place, first frame and being in play before both had it compared as ever (BN6's spark ends 2 frames before BN4's, t72 against t74 in walla_v1)

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's paralysis state's flag 0x400000
allowed.why: BN6's own bookkeeping in its own MegaMan's paralysis state, not the port's subject (the lead's call, 2026-11-04, the owner's to overturn). Its writer: BN6's paralysis state (his state 4, entry 4 of his table 0x080EB86C: 0x080175B8) sets 0x400000 in his collision flags as it begins (0x080175C4: ldr r0,=0x400000; bl 0x0801A152); its clearer: 0x08017828 (in 0x08017768, his state 7, entry 7 of that table: bl 0x0801A15C); its reader: 0x08010162, run for him each frame from 0x0801B12E, which clears the flags' 0x04 while 0x400000 stands and sets it else (0x08010182-0x08010192). BN4's paralysis state (0x080109FA, entry 4 of his table 0x080EAEFC) sets no 0x400000: as it begins it clears 0x100441 as BN6's does (0x08010A0A / 0x080175CA), and no load of 0x400000 is in its code. Both set and clear 0x800 alike (the status routines 0x0800AEB4 / 0x0800E798, the ends 0x0800AE6C / 0x0800E74C). BN6's struck state (his state 3, entry 3 of 0x080EB86C: 0x080174FE) sets it too, with 0x400, as it begins (0x0801750A: ldr r0,=0x400400; bl 0x0801A152) and clears both as it ends (0x0801758A: bl 0x0801A15C), where BN4's (0x08010960, entry 3 of 0x080EAEFC) sets and clears 0x400 alone (0x0801096C-0x08010970: movs r0,#1; lsls r0,#10; bl 0x08012F82; 0x080109DE-0x080109E2, bl 0x08012F8C): walla_v1-v3, MegaMan struck by Walla's rings, 23 frames a hit. Guarded: that bit alone, BN6's side holding it and BN4's not, every other bit of the word compared as ever, the 0x04 it acts on among them, so any effect it had on him would still fail the spec or keep it INCONCLUSIVE (tools/xdiff_bn4.py allowed_world)

allowed.name: a Navi's actor type and AI index, BN6's
allowed.why: BN6's battle actor setup writes the enemy id's triple +1, its actor type (1 a Navi), at AI data +0 and its +2, the AI index, at +1 (0x08007720-0x08007726, r4 the AI data), which BN6 reads to pick a triple's word (its spawn hooks, 0x0800F420: ldr r3,[r5,#0x58]; ldrb r1,[r3,#0]; ldrb r1,[r3,#1]) and its palette (0x0800F334), and its Navi frame reads its thirteen tables by (BN6_NAVI_FRAME, AIData +1: GutsMan's 49, src/emu/xnavi_recipe.h XN_BN4_FIRST_AI). BN4 has no triples and no Navi tables (a Navi its own first-kind type, BN4_T1_TYPES); its Navi's AI data is its side's (BN4_AI_OF_SIDE), whose +0 and +1 GutsMan's code and the engine's routines his states call never read (tools/xnavirecipe_bn4.py's AI tracker: his reads are his blocks, +0x64 on): BN6's own bookkeeping

allowed.name: a Navi's level by its foe's HP, BN6's
allowed.why: BN6's actor init writes AI data +0xC the other side's 0x080136E4(side ^ 1, 0x3E) / 100, 1 to 10 (0x08017068-0x08017088): MegaMan's 2000 HP gives 10 in gutsman_v1. BN4's AI data +0xC is a player's loadout (BN4_AI_LOADOUT), 0 on a Navi's side, never read by GutsMan's code (his AI tracker's reads): BN6's own

allowed.name: a Navi's AI data +0xE, BN6's
allowed.why: BN6's battle actor setup writes 0xFF at AI data +0xE (0x08007764-0x08007766). BN4's +0xE (a player's loadout's chip charge, BN4_AI_LOADOUT + 2) is 0 on a Navi's side and never read by GutsMan's code: BN6's own

allowed.name: a Navi's version, BN6's
allowed.why: BN6's battle actor setup writes its enemy id's triple +0 (0x080182B4, r0 the id) at AI data +0x16 and +0x17 (0x0800771A-0x0800771E), which for a moved Navi's ids is its version (src/emu/xnavi_install.c ids_set: { v, 1, ai }): 0 for V1, so no V1 spec saw it; roll_v2 shows 1, roll_v3 2, roll_sp 3. BN6's code that reads it for a Navi: the actor init's palette (0x0800F334: BN6_NAVI_PALETTE_VERSIONS, 0x0800F354, its byte by the version times the step, 0 for versions 0-3, so V1's palette for every one) and the per-version table reads 0x0800FE12 and 0x0800FE36, which BN6's own Navis call and no call of a BN4 Navi's recipe names (src/emu/xnavi_bn4.c); a scan of BN6's ROM for ldrb at +0x16 or +0x17 within eight halfwords of a load from the object's +0x58 found those three engine routines and per-Navi and per-virus code past 0x0809E000 alone. BN4's +0x16 and +0x17 of a Navi's side's AI data (BN4_AI_OF_SIDE) stay 0, and Roll's code reads her AI data out of its blocks at +0x9-+0xB, +0x30 and +0x32 alone (tools/xnavirecipe_bn4.py's AI tracker), its blocks from +0x64: BN6's own

allowed.name: a Navi's target, BN6's
allowed.why: BN6 keeps an actor's target object at AI data +0x78 (0x0800F318: str r0,[r1,#0x78], r1 its AI data), MegaMan's for GutsMan. BN4's +0x78 is in his attack's variables (BN4_AI_ATTACK_VARS + 8), traced at BN6's +0xA8 (src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c's ai_segs), so BN4's trace holds nothing at BN6's +0x78: BN6's own

allowed.name: a Navi's AI data's pool bit, BN6's
allowed.why: BN6's AI data comes from a pool of eight, each entry's own bit at +0x7C (bn6_ai.h BN6_AI_POOL_BIT: entry i bit 31 - i, laid out by the take 0x0800ED2C; GutsMan's entry 1, 0x40000000, +0x7F 0x40), which its let-go clears (0x0800ED80). BN4 has no pool, one AI data a side (BN4_AI_DATA): BN6's own

allowed.name: a side's control block, BN4's
allowed.why: BN4's AI data +0x50 points at its side's control block (BN4_AI_CONTROL, set as the battle clears each side's AI data, 0x0800B7CE), a Navi's side's as MegaMan's; BN6's AI pool entry for a Navi holds none (its take zeroes +0 to +0x7B, 0x0800ED2C), and GutsMan's code never reads it (his AI tracker's reads): BN4's own

allowed.name: GutsMan's attack's spawn's r3, each game's leftover
allowed.why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r1, r2 and r3 at the object's +0x34, +0x38 and +0x3C and r4 at +4, as BN6's twin through the dispatch's spawner does; GutsMan's spawner of his attack's 0x1C (0x080D0894: push {r0,r1,r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x1c; the spawn) sets r0 alone, so +0x3C holds what r3 held before it: in BN4 the battle state's pointer, in BN6 3. No code of the 0x1C object reads +0x3C (its init 0x080D057C and update 0x080D058E and the routines they reach, walked by tools/xnavirecipe_bn4.py), nor do the engine's routines it calls

allowed.name: the explosions' maker's spawn's r2, each game's leftover
allowed.why: The fourth kind's spawn stores the caller's r2 at the object's +0x38 (with r1 at +0x34 and r3 at +0x3C). SeekBom's bomb (BN4's third kind's 0x8D, moved with its unit) spawns the explosions' maker (the fourth kind's 0x11) as a hit ends it, through the maker's spawner with r4 alone set (movs r4,#2; bl 0x080E33D4 at 0x080DEE20), after its update loaded r1 and r0 (0x080DEDFA-0x080DEDFC) and nothing r2: r2 is what the collision step before it left (BN4 0x080129FC, BN6's own 0x0801A00E, neither the bomb's code), 8 in BN4's and 0x88 in BN6's. No code of the maker loads its +0x38 (its init copies its parent's place to its +0x60 on, 0x080E3352-0x080E335C, and its step reads +0x60: 0x080E33A2). bn4_chip_seekbom1 at t83

allowed.name: the explosions' maker's spawn's r1, the bomb's collision data's address
allowed.why: The fourth kind's spawn stores the caller's r1 at the object's +0x34. SeekBom's bomb spawns the explosions' maker right after its update loaded its own collision data's address into r1 (ldr r1,[r5,#0x54] at 0x080DEDFA, for the flags it tests at 0x080DEDFC-0x080DEE00), so +0x34 holds that address: while the bomb lives the comparison reads it as the bomb's collision data in both, and once the bomb is freed as each engine's own address of it (BN4 0x02039B30, BN6 0x02038640: each game's collision pool's entry for the bomb, the same in every spec of the unit). No code of the maker loads its +0x34 (its init takes its place from its parent, 0x080E3352-0x080E335C). bn4_chip_seekbom2 from t84

allowed.name: ThunderMan's 0x70's spawn's r4, each game's leftover
allowed.why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r4 at the object's +4, as BN6's twin through the dispatch's spawner does; ThunderMan's spawner of his 0x70 (0x080DB524: push {r0,r1,r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x70; the spawn) sets r0 alone, and its one caller, his state 87 (MegaMan's in BN4, copied with him: 0x080F23DC, its bl at 0x080F23EE) sets r0 to r2 before it, so +4 holds what r4 held as each game's state runner called the state: in BN4 0x13, in BN6 his AI data's address. No code 0x70 runs reads its +4 to +7: its type routine (0x080DB3F8), init (0x080DB41C), update (0x080DB464) and dying (0x08010560) and the 21 routines they call, walked (tools/xrecipe_thumb.py) for a load of +4 to +7 from any register, find one alone, the object free's (0x080033FA), which reads its list node's link (r0 its record less 0x10). thunderman_v1 at t277 (BN4) and t278 (BN6)

allowed.name: ThunderMan's 0x71's spawn's r4, each game's leftover
allowed.why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r4 at the object's +4 as a word; ThunderMan's spawner of his 0x71 (0x080DB6CE: push {r4,lr}; push {r0-r3,r5}; movs r0,#0x71; the spawn) then writes +4's byte alone from the caller's r3 (0x080DB6E0, strb r4,[r0,#4] after pop {r1-r5}), and its one caller, his state 85 (MegaMan's in BN4, copied with him: its bl at 0x080F22B2, r3 0 at 0x080F22B0) leaves r4 what the state runner held (its pop {r4} at 0x080F22A6), so +5 to +7 hold its upper bytes: in BN4 0 (0x13), in BN6 his AI data's address's (0x41, 0x03 at +5 and +6). No code 0x71 runs reads its +5 to +7: its type routine (0x080DB540), init (0x080DB564), update (0x080DB5CE) and dying (0x08010560) and the 61 routines they call, walked (tools/xrecipe_thumb.py) for a load of +4 to +7 from any register, find only other records' (its collision data's +5 and +7, a panel's +4, a list node's +4, the spawn's descriptor's +4). thunderman_v1 from t740 (BN4) and t741 (BN6)

allowed.name: JunkMan's junk's spawn's r4, each game's leftover
allowed.why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r4 at the object's +4 as a word, as BN6's twin through the dispatch's spawner does; JunkMan's spawner of his junk, the third kind's 0x96 (0x080DFF60: push {r4,lr}; push {r0-r3,r5}; movs r0,#0x96; the spawn), sets r0 alone, and its one caller, his update's call before his state runner (0x080C94AE, its bl at 0x080C9562), leaves r4 as his update was entered: in BN4 his +0 byte as BN4's object runner read it (0x13), in BN6 his AI index times four as BN6's Navi frame keeps it across his hook A (0x080F3682: lsls r4,r0,#2; AI 57, 0xE4; his hook A's shim pushes and pops r4, src/emu/xnavi_init.c pre_set). +5 to +7 hold r4's upper bytes, 0 in both. No code 0x96 runs reads its +4 to +7: its block (0x080DFD54-0x080DFF8C: its type routine 0x080DFD54, init 0x080DFD74, update 0x080DFDF2, the hits test and the spawner past them), read for a load or store of +4 to +7 through r5, has none, and its dying is the families' (0x08010560, ThunderMan's 0x70's walk). This byte pair alone, on that object; junkman_v1 at t1 (BN4) and t2 (BN6)

allowed.name: BN6's support attack's end, a frame after its routine
allowed.subject: megaman
allowed.why: Each game's support family runs the chip's routine from the subfamilies' table (BN4 0x080EB9EA from 0x080220E0, BN6 0x080ED0DC from 0x0802CCB4, by bx r3). BN4's ends the attack in the same frame (bl 0x0800C9FC at 0x080EBA36, straight after the routine's result is stored); BN6's stores 1 in the attack's phase (movs r0,#1; strb r0,[r7,#1] at 0x080ED12A) and ends it the frame after, by that phase (ldrb r0,[r7,#1]; cmp r0,#0; bne at 0x080ED0DE to bl 0x08011714 at 0x080ED130). So on that one frame BN6's MegaMan still holds the support family (CurAction 0x15) with phase 1 where BN4's is back in his own state: his CurAction and the phase byte alone, there alone (tools/xdiff_bn4.py support_end). And from the next frame his own record of BN6's is a frame further behind BN4's than the battle is (megaman_clock: read that frame later, his object and AI data, what his state runner drives; his collision data and his object's visible bit, +0's 0x02, stay the battle's frame's, the status routines' by the collision data's timers: an invisibility's count and its blink, bn4_chip_invis; nothing else of the battle), until the world gives him a state (below). BN6's own support chips hold him so too: the engine's, not the chip's. bn4_chip_areagrab at t33, his records alike from t34 to t121 read so

allowed.name: MegaMan's clock rejoining the battle's at a state the world gives him
allowed.subject: megaman
allowed.why: A hit lands at the battle's frame in both games (the hit's state, the engine's generic 3, set by each game's hit pass on the frame the attack's collision meets his), not by his own clock: so BN6's record of his own clock, read a frame later (above), shows the state a frame before BN4's does, and BN4's one frame between, his last in his own state, has no twin in BN6's (where he was a frame behind and the hit cut that frame). Held to exactly that: BN6's later record in a generic state (0 to 5, numbered alike), BN4's not in it now and in it at its next frame; his records are not compared on that frame alone and are read with the battle's offset again from the next. bn4_chip_areagrab at t122: the Mettaur's wave hits him at t123 in both

allowed.name: SearchMan's trail's 'begun', each game's PlaySound's leftover r0
allowed.why: His shots' trail, the fourth kind's 0x31 moved with him, runs its kind 0 (0x080E5960) by a 'begun' byte at its +9: where it reads 0 (0x080E5968-0x080E596C) it plays its sound (movs r0,#0x29; adds r0,#0xff; bl PlaySoundEffect at 0x080E5976) and stores the r0 that call leaves at +9 (strb r0,[r5,#9] at 0x080E597A), then never reads +9 but for that test. PlaySoundEffect (BN4 0x08000560, BN6 0x080005CC: push {r1-r7,lr}, the song's start, pop) restores every register but r0, which holds what each game's own MP2K song start left (BN4's through 0x08112849, BN6's through 0x08150475; BN6's call through his home's sound shim, XvSoundCall, to the same routine): 0x28 in BN4, 0x48 in BN6, both not 0, so the trail's kind 0 runs alike. This byte pair alone, on that object; searchman_v1 at t740 (BN4) and t741 (BN6)

allowed.name: WoodMan's 0x94's spawn's r2, each game's camera
allowed.why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r1, r2 and r3 at the object's +0x34, +0x38 and +0x3C, as BN6's twin through the dispatch's spawner does; WoodMan's spawner of his 0x94 (0x080DFA38: push {lr}; push {r5}; movs r0,#0x94; the spawn) sets r0 alone, and its one caller, his state 106 (MegaMan's in BN4, copied with him: its bl at 0x080F4D3C), calls the camera's shake set just before it (0x080F4D2A, BN4_CAMERA_SHAKE_SET 0x0802608C, BN6's 0x080302A8 the same body: mov r2,r10; ldr r2,[r2,#0xc], its stores), so +0x38 holds each game's camera, [r10 +0xC]: 0x02009B80 in BN4, 0x02009180 in BN6. No code 0x94 runs reads its +0x34 to +0x3F: its block (0x080DF9B0-0x080DFA78, its type routine, states and spawner of 0x95) walked for a load of them finds none, and its calls (GetRNG 0x08001B16, the pause test 0x08007A12, the after-step 0x080143FC, 0x080DFA64 and the 0x95 spawner 0x080DFCA4) read its +4, +0x16, +0x17, +0x2C and +0x4C alone (the loads of +0x34 and +0x38 at 0x080DFBC6-0x080DFD18 are 0x95's own states', on a 0x95). This word alone, on that object; woodman_v1 at t43

allowed.name: BN6's Elec tally of a hit, its freeze's
allowed.why: BN6's own bookkeeping for its freeze, which BN4 has none of: BN6's hit pass (its image 0x081D78F6-0x081D7904) adds the attack's damage (+0x2E) to the struck's +0x78 where the attack's element (+2) is 3, Elec, before its damage by element (BN6_COLL_HIT_DAMAGES, +0x82 + 2 * element: 0x081D7906-0x081D7910), and the frame's step adds +0x78 to the Elec hit damage (+0x88) while the struck's +6 is 8 (0x0801A8E0-0x0801A8F6: an Elec hit on a frozen one counts twice). BN4's hit pass (0x08012C74-0x08012C82) has the damage by element alone (BN4_COLL_HIT_DAMAGES, +0x2A + 2 * element), no test of the element 3 and no store of a tally. thunderman_v1 at t278 (BN4) and t279 (BN6): his 0x70's Elec hit, 0x32 at BN6's +0x78 alone, the damage by element the same in both (+0x88 and +0x9A, BN4's +0x30 and +0x42); MegaMan's HP the same in all 1200 fight frames. Guarded: those two bytes, BN6's side holding something and BN4's 0, every other field compared

allowed.name: the wind's spawner, BN6's
allowed.fields: the wind's (the fourth kind's 0x41) +0x4C alone, only where BN4's is 0 and BN6's names the moved Navi whose decision spawned it (tools/xdiff_bn4.py spawner_kept); every other byte of the wind compared as ever
allowed.why: A Navi's wind is each engine's own fourth-kind 0x41, spawned by twin routines (BN4_WIND_SPAWN 0x080E68F8, BN6_WIND_SPAWN 0x080E666C: the side's slot read, the spawn, the side copied, +0's 0x10 cleared, the slot set) but for one store: BN6's keeps its spawner at the wind's +0x4C (0x080E6692: str r5,[r0,#0x4c]), BN4's has none (0x080E690C-0x080E6930), so BN4's +0x4C is the 0 its spawn's clear left. BN6's wind reads it in its state 4 (0x080E65BA: its step 0x080E65D6 skipped while the spawner's CurAction is 4, ldr r0,[r5,#0x4c]; ldrb r0,[r0,#9], or its collision data's +0x3C holds 0x80010000, the literal at 0x080E67AC), and BN4's wind runs its step unasked (0x080E6858 to 0x080E6860); the port calls BN6's spawn (WindMan's decision's call of BN4_WIND_SPAWN aimed at its twin), so BN6's wind has the owner its own state 4 dereferences. Both of WindMan's states 4 (his paralysis) and 3 end the wind first (BN4_WIND_END, +8 8), so the hold differs only in a frame where his CurAction is 4 before his state 4 has run, or his collision holds those flags: no spec reaches either yet (windman_v1's MegaMan idle)

allowed.name: WindMan's wind's spawn's r3, each game's leftover
allowed.why: The fourth kind's spawn (BN4 0x08003344, BN6 0x080033AC, through 0x08003210 / 0x08003278) keeps the caller's r1 to r3 at the object's +0x34 to +0x3C, as the third kind's does (GutsMan's attack's spawn's r3, above). WindMan's wind is spawned by BN4_WIND_SPAWN (0x080E68F8; BN6's twin 0x080E666C, the port's call) from his decision (0x080C336C) and from his attack, MegaMan's state 64 of BN4 (0x080F0BF4-0x080F0C08: the old wind ended through 0x080E69BC, which writes r1 alone, then r4 0 and the spawn); the slot's reader before the spawn (0x080E69E8 / 0x080E677C) sets r0 to r2, so +0x3C holds the r3 the state was run with: in BN4 the battle state's pointer, in BN6 3 (windman_v1's second wind, t103 in BN4 and t104 in BN6, as GutsMan's attack's). No code of the wind reads its own +0x3C: its routine and states (BN4 0x080E6820-0x080E6A20, BN6 0x080E6584-0x080E67A0) and the routines they call, two calls deep, hold no load of [r5,#0x3c] (BN6's 0x080E65C8 reads its spawner's collision data's +0x3C)

allowed.name: Roll's flash's spawn's r4, each game's leftover

No code of the flash reads its +4 to +7: its routine (0x080E3A98-0x080E3AD6) loads +0xB, +0x20 and +0x34 to +0x3C alone, and the routines it calls take their registers alone (0x08014620, a jitter of r1 and r3 by a draw; BN4_SPAWN_EFFECT 0x080E18EE, BN6's twin 0x080E1932, r4 its effect; the object's free 0x080033D4). roll_v1 at t66 (BN4) and t67 (BN6)

allowed.name: a summoned Mettaur's +0xF, BN4's appear queue's number
allowed.why: BN4's spawn of an enemy into a fight under way (BN4_SPAWN_ENEMY, Roll's summon) writes its enemy id at its +0xF (0x080F0158), which the BN4 trace moves to BN6's NameID (+0x28, src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c obj_segs), and its appear queue's number at its +0xE (0x080F015A-0x080F0164: the battle state's +9, then that counter one up; BN4_QUEUE_ENTER keeps objects' +0xE bytes), which the trace moves to the first place its layout leaves, +0xF (xd4_translate's second pass: BN6's element takes +0xE, BN4's +0x17). So BN4's side reads the summon's number in the battle there: 1 for her first summon, 2 for her second (roll_v2_summons: Mettaur2 1 at t998, Billy2 2 at t2050; not the enemy id, which roll_v1's Mettaur V1, id 1, read as 1 by chance). BN6's spawn of one (BN6_SPAWN_ENEMY_1, the summon's shim's) keeps its appear queue as object pointers (BN6_QUEUE_*) and leaves +0xF 0, a byte BN6's own generic states keep a count in (0x08016716). No code of BN4's Mettaur or Billy, moved, reads its +0xE (their appear queue calls go through the queue shims to BN6's queues of pointers, bn4_twins.QUEUED) nor +0xF: this pair alone, so a write of either engine's after the spawn still parts

allowed.name: the wind's gust's sprite flag 0x80, BN6's
allowed.why: A wind's gust is each engine's own third-kind 0x49, spawned by the engine's wind (BN4's fourth-kind 0x41, its update's bl at 0x080E68C2 to 0x080D68AC; BN6's at 0x080E6636 to 0x080CECF8), its init twins (BN4 0x080D6748, BN6 0x080CEB80) but for one immediate: sprite_load writes its caller's r0 at the sprite state's +3 (BN4 0x0800288E push {r0,r1,r2} to 0x080028B6 strb r1,[r5,#3]; BN6 0x080026F6 to 0x0800271E, the same steps), and BN6's init passes 0x80 (movs r0,#0x80 at 0x080CEB90) where BN4's passes the r0 its +0 flags left (0x080D6750-0x080D6756: ldrb, orrs #2, strb). Its object's +0x93 is that byte: BN4 0x0E, BN6 0x8E (windman_v1 at t1, the gust of WindMan's first wind). With BN6's immediate made 0 (--poke 080CEB90:2000:2) +0x93 is alike at t1 and no other record of the battle moves. That bit alone, BN6's, on that object; its other bits compared as ever

allowed.name: a native's own art, the same bytes
allowed.fields: a world's object of a type each engine runs as its own (not moved: the gust above), its sprite state's words into its sprite (+0x18 to +0x27 of its state: the sprite + 4, its frame's records) alone, only where each game's last sprite set-up of it (the hooks' sprite events) has the same bytes (CRC32) and the same list and number, each word read by its offset from its sprite's start and alike where the offsets are (tools/xdiff_bn4.py own_art); every other byte of its sprite state compared as ever
allowed.why: Each engine draws its own object from its own ROM's sprite lists (sprite_load, BN4 0x0800287C, BN6 0x080026E4: the list's entry + 4 at the state's +0x18, 0x080028C4 / 0x0800272C, its frames' records found from there), so a pointer into the art is each game's own address of the same bytes: the wind's gust's (list 0xC, number 0x2E: CRC32 0xE0F284B6 in both, the hooks' sprite events from BN4 0x080D6761 and BN6 0x080CEB9B) at BN4 0x0837FBC8 and BN6 0x08324390, windman_v1 at t1. Read by the offset into the same bytes, it is the same frame of the same art; a different picture, list or number, or another frame of it, still parts

allowed.name: BN6's MegaMan's step's kind
allowed.why: BN6 keeps the kind of a step an object takes at its +0x0F: its step onto a panel begun (BN6_STEP_BEGIN 0x0801AD12: collision flags 0x100 and 4, then movs r0,#1; strb r0,[r5,#0xf] at 0x0801AD5C; four more steps alike, 0x0801AC2E, 0x0801ADEE, 0x0801AE4A, 0x0801AEF2) sets it, its slide's end clears it (0x08016804-0x08016806), and its slide's step reads it as the row of its table (0x0800E468: ldrb r0,[r5,#0xf] at 0x0800E46C, into 0x0800E498's table at 0x0800E4AC). BN4's twin of the step (BN4_STEP_BEGIN 0x0801393E, the symbol map's pair) sets the same collision flags (0x08013988-0x08013992) and no byte of the object's, and BN4's slide's step (0x0800ACAA) takes its row from the collision data's push bits (+0xD, 0x0800ACB2) instead. BN4's +0x0F is its enemy id's byte, read as BN6's NameID by the trace, so BN4's side holds 0 there. windman_v1: MegaMan's +0x0F 1 in BN6 alone while the gust pushes him a column (t4-t7) and while his wind pulls him two (t882-t889), his place, panels and every other byte the same in both. His alone, BN6's side only where BN4's holds 0

allowed.name: MegaMan's blocked slide's step, BN4's
allowed.why: A slide begun (BN4 0x08010294, BN6 0x080166D0, twins) stores its step's panels to go, column and row (+0x1B, +0x1C, +0x1D: strb r2, r0, r1 at BN4 0x080102B6-0x080102BA, BN6 0x080166F2-0x080166F6) from each game's step routine. BN6's (0x0800E468) tests the panel the step leads to inside it (bl 0x0800E5AC at 0x0800E480) and returns zeros where it cannot be entered (0x0800E486-0x0800E48A); BN4's (0x0800ACAA) returns the step its collision's push bits name whatever the panel, and its slide tests the panel after (bl 0x0800ACF4 at 0x080102CC), its blocked slide ending with the step kept. So where the wind pushes MegaMan against the field's edge BN4 holds the step and BN6 zeros: windman_v1 from t9 (BN4 6, 0xFF, 0 against 0, 0, 0, MegaMan on column 1 pushed left) and from t891 (6, 1, 0: on column 3 pulled right); a slide that moves him stores the same step in both (t4, t882). His alone, BN4's side only where BN6's holds 0

allowed.name: a slide's direction, each engine's clock
allowed.fields: MegaMan's collision data's last move's direction (+0x0C, BN6_COLL_PANEL_BYTE; BN4's +0x0A read as BN6's, tools/xdiff_bn4.py direction_as_bn6) alone, only where one game holds 0 and the other the direction of his last move read as BN6's from BN4's own trace (MOVES; slide_direction); every other value of it compared as ever
allowed.why: Both games write the direction of an object's move from its old panel to its new at the collision data's panel byte, by different clocks for a slide: BN4's collision panels' update (0x08012D9A, BN4_DIRECTION at 0x08012DAE), called by the slide at its start and end (0x080102A6, 0x08010390) and each frame, writes it on the frame his panel changes and 0 on the next; BN6's slide writes it once at its end from its step (0x080167E6-0x080167F6: bl 0x0801683C with +0x1C, +0x1D and his side, strb r0,[r1,#0xc]) and keeps it until another move or hit writes it (its collision panels' update, 0x0801A04C, is not run by the slide's steps). windman_v1: BN4 3 at t7 only, BN6 3 from t8 to t657 (MegaMan pushed from column 2 to 1); BN4 4 at t884 and t888, BN6 4 from t890 to t1014 (pulled from 1 to 3). The value is the same move's in both, read by BN6's rule; only when it is held differs

allowed.name: a slid foe's blocked slide's step, BN4's
allowed.fields: a first-kind object of the family's in a chip's spec (subject megaman: the chip's foe), its slide's step (+0x1B, +0x1C, +0x1D) alone, only where BN6's holds 0 (tools/xdiff_bn4.py foe_slide); the slide's counts (+0x1E, +0x1F), its panels and its state compared as ever
allowed.why: The entry "MegaMan's blocked slide's step, BN4's" on a foe: a slide is the engine's for any first-kind object, begun by the same routine (BN4 0x08010294, BN6 0x080166D0), and each engine's only stores to an object's +0x1B are that routine's and its steps' (a search of both engines' code for strb to [r5,#0x1b]: BN4 0x080102BA, 0x08010330, 0x0801034E, 0x08010354; BN6 0x080166F6, 0x08016764, 0x080167AE, 0x080167B6). BN6's step routine (0x0800E468) tests the panel the step leads to and returns zeros where it cannot be entered; BN4's (0x0800ACAA) returns the step whatever the panel and its slide tests the panel after (bl 0x0800ACF4 at 0x080102CC), ending with the step kept. MagBolt2's hit pulls a Mettaur on column 4 toward MegaMan's panels, which it cannot enter: BN4 holds 6, 0xFF, 0 from the hit's frame (bn4_chip_magbolt2, t40 on) and BN6 zeros, the Mettaur on (4,2) in both. A pull that moves the foe stores the same step in both (bn4_chip_magbolt1, the Mettaur from (5,2) to (4,2): 6, 0xFF, 0 and the counts 4, 4 down to 1 in both)

allowed.name: a slid foe's slide's direction, each engine's clock
allowed.fields: the same object's collision data's last move's direction (+0x0C, BN6_COLL_PANEL_BYTE; BN4's +0x0A read as BN6's, direction_as_bn6) alone, only where one game holds 0 and the other the direction of its last move read as BN6's from BN4's own trace (MOVES; slide_direction with the foe's role); every other value of it compared as ever
allowed.why: The entry "a slide's direction, each engine's clock" on a foe, the same code: BN4's collision panels' update (0x08012D9A), called by the slide at its start and end and each frame, writes the direction on the frame the object's panel changes and 0 on the next; BN6's slide writes it once at its end from its step (0x080167E6-0x080167F6) and keeps it. bn4_chip_magbolt1: the Mettaur pulled from (5,2) to (4,2), BN4's 4 (its 3 read by the side) at t43 alone, BN6's 4 from t44 on. The value is the same move's in both; only when it is held differs

allowed.name: a struck foe's blocked push's step, BN4's
allowed.fields: the same object's +0x0B alone, only while both games hold it in the struck-and-pushed state (its +0x09 5 in both) and BN6's holds 0 (tools/xdiff_bn4.py foe_slide)
allowed.why: The struck-and-pushed state's first phase (the engine's state 5: BN4 0x080105DC, BN6's twin) asks the same step routine as a slide and stores its panels to go at the object's +0x0B (BN4 strb r2,[r5,#0xb] at 0x08010610, with +0x1C and +0x1D at 0x0801060C-0x0801060E). BN4's routine (0x0800ACAA) returns the step whatever the panel, the state testing the panel after (bl 0x0800ACF4 at 0x08010622) and waiting 0x18 frames where it cannot be entered (0x0801064E-0x08010654); BN6's (0x0800E468) returns zeros there: the entry "MegaMan's blocked slide's step, BN4's", at this state's place. bn4_chip_magbolt3: the Mettaur, pulled beside MegaMan and struck toward his panels, holds 6 in BN4's and 0 in BN6's from t44 to t68, its state's 0x18 frames, the same frames in both

allowed.name: a foe struck on its slide's last step, each runner's order
allowed.fields: the same object's slide's phase and counts (+0x1B, +0x1E, +0x1F) alone, only where BN4's record is a slide ended (5, 0, 0) and BN6's the slide with one step left (+0x1B 6, +0x1E 1); its panels, its state and its timers compared as ever
allowed.why: A virus's runner runs a pushed object's slide and then takes a struck-and-pushed hit in BN4, and the other way round in BN6. BN4's (0x08013E3C on): the pushed status 0x10 or the slide's flag 0x1000 runs the slide's step (bl 0x08010F00 at 0x08013E4C and 0x08013E5E), then status 0x100 makes its state 5 (0x08013E68 on). BN6's: status 0x100 makes its state 5 (0x0801B2A8-0x0801B2D2) and branches past the slide's step (b 0x0801B338 at 0x0801B2D4; the step, bl 0x080166B6, at 0x0801B2FC and 0x0801B30E). So a hit that strikes and pushes on the frame of a slide's last step finds the step run in BN4 (its phase 5, its counts 0) and not in BN6 (6, one step left of four frames), the object on its new panel in both, which the step before set. Nothing reads the leftover: the state clears the slide's flag itself (BN4 0x080105F6-0x080105F8, 0x1000) and the next slide begun stores all of them. bn4_chip_magbolt3: the Mettaur pulled from (5,2) to (4,2), the bolt's hit with the pull's on the slide's fourth frame, t44; HP 10, state 5 and its end at t69 the same in both

allowed.name: BN6's second wheel in MegaMan's chip's attack, the Cursor's
allowed.why: As a chip is used BN6 writes his AttackVars +2 (AI data +0xA2) as the chip record's attack element ORed with its icon's second-wheel element's hit flag (Sword 0x80, Cursor 0x40, Wind 0x20, Break 0x10: BN6's table 0x080129E4 by the record's +6), where BN4's use writes the attack element alone (0x0800D4D2 on: its record's +4 into +2; BN4 has no second wheel). A BN4 chip's record in a run holds BN4's kind as BN6's icon element (src/core/xchips_record.c xrec_from_bn4, BN4 numbering its kinds as BN5 its icon elements: its 8 the Cursor, BN6's 6), as BN5's chips' do (masks, "BN6's second wheel in a chip's attack"): BN6's engine's own flag for its second wheel's weaknesses, the bit BN6 has and BN4 not, that bit alone. The Cursor's, PanlSht's kind; another kind's flag is another entry, with its chip's spec.
evidence: BN6 0x0801271E-0x08012728 (the chip's numbers written for its attack, 0x080126E4): ldrb r1,[r6,#4]; ldrb r2,[r6,#6]; ldr r0,=0x080129E4; ldrb r0,[r0,r2]; orrs r1,r0; strb r1,[r7,#2]

allowed.name: BN6's second wheel in the panel shot's object's spawn's r2

allowed.name: the boomerang's +0x4C, each game's sprite update's leftover r2
allowed.why: Boomer's boomerang's init (BN4's third-kind 0x32, moved with Boomer's unit) stores r2 at +0x4C (str r2,[r5,#0x4c] at 0x080D32AA) after its sprite's update (bl 0x0800283C at 0x080D3282; BN6's twin 0x080026A4 through the copy's veneer), which nothing between sets: each game's update's leftover there, 0 in BN4's and a pointer into the sprite in BN6's. allowed.name: the Moko's hit's bits, struck and pushed in each engine's own
allowed.why: MokoRus's Moko (BN4's third-kind 0x2C, moved with MokoRus's unit) sets up its collision with r3 0x21 (movs r3,#0x21 at 0x080D23E0, bl 0x080129AC), the hit's bits the hit pass ORs into the struck's (BN4 0x08012C40-0x08012C46, BN6 0x081D7830 on). BN4's struck pass of the first kind makes a hit struck and pushed of bit 0x01 with a push bit, 0xFC (0x0801360C-0x08013622: status 0x100 set, the flinch's 0x4 cleared); BN6's of bit 0x40 with a push bit, 0x3C (0x0801AC06-0x0801AC2E: the same two stores), and of a push bit without 0x40 it pushes alone (status 0x10, 0x0801AC32-0x0801AC3E). So the copy's init passes 0x61 (tools/xchiprecipe_bn4.py IMMS), BN6's bits for the same hit: with BN4's 0x21 there BN6's Mettaur is pushed back and goes on with its attack where BN4's is struck (bn4_chip_mokorus1 at t93, its state 5 in BN4's and 0xB in BN6's). The struck's own records, its HP, its panel and its states, are compared as ever.

allowed.name: MegaMan's dark palette, BN4's
allowed.why: MegaMan's palette (his object's +0x94, his sprite state's +4) while his karma is dark: BN4 gives his look by his karma as his battle begins and again as his state calls for it (0x0800BFFE, from his init 0x080107DE and seven more callers, into BN4_SPRITE_PALETTE_SET 0x08002DEC), 2, his own sprite's dark colours, where the karma is under 470 (0x0800C052: 4 from 1000, 0 from 500, 3 from 470, 2 under it; a spec's karma4 of 480 shows 0 there all battle, which the karma's own steps at 480 and 500, 0x0800F5BC, may explain: not read further, and no pair but 2 against 0 is allowed). BN6's MegaMan has no karma and no dark palette (0x0801002C, the twin, gives 1 under the chip AI, 4 at Full Synchro, else 0): a run takes no karma, and his dark look is not taken (docs/game/meta/darkchips.md, BN4's dark chips: the price is the whole of their darkness). It arises only where a spec gives BN4's battle a dark karma (karma4 under 470: a dark chip played in BN4's own battle). That pair alone; everything else of him compared as ever.
evidence: BN4 0x080107DE bl 0x0800BFFE, then 0x080107E2 bl BN4_SPRITE_PALETTE_SET (strb r0 at the sprite state's +4, 0x08002DF4)
BN6 0x0801002C: 1 where AIData +0x48's 0x200 (0x0801004C), 4 where his mood is 0xFF (0x08010070), 0 else (0x08010076); no karma read
bn4_chip_invis_dark: Invis by a dark MegaMan (karma4 0), his +0x94 2 in BN4 from the first frame, 0 in BN6, nothing else of the battle apart

allowed.name: MagBolt's bolt's hit's bits, struck and pushed in each engine's own
allowed.why: MagBolt's bolt (BN4's third-kind 0x75, moved with MagBolt's unit) sets up its collision with r3 3 (movs r3,#3 at 0x080DBCD2, bl 0x080129AC), and its hit lands with the pull's, the state's hit of bits 0x08 each frame (0x080EE10C's word 0x1E05FF08 through 0x080CD7E2): the struck holds 0x0B. BN4's struck pass makes that struck and pushed by bit 0x01 with a push bit (0x0801360C-0x08013622), BN6's by bit 0x40 with one (0x0801AC06-0x0801AC2E), the entry "the Moko's hit's bits, struck and pushed in each engine's own". So the copy's init passes 0x43 (tools/xchiprecipe_bn4.py IMMS): with BN4's 3 there BN6's Mettaur, pulled beside MegaMan and hit, goes on with its own state where BN4's is struck (bn4_chip_magbolt3 at t44, its state 5 in BN4's and 0xB in BN6's). The struck's own records are compared as ever.

bn4.clocks: Two clocks, each record's proven from the routine that writes it, never assumed (the lead's call, 2026-11-04, the owner's to overturn). What a state drives (an object's state routine, run by its state runner: BN4 0x08013C48, BN6 0x0801B1C4) is compared with the battle's offset, BN6's at t + 1 against BN4's at t (allowed, "BN6's battle a fight frame behind BN4's"); what the battle's timer or the frame counter drives (a routine the main loop runs each fight frame, not through a state) at the same fight frame. Each record of the second clock is named with its code path (bn4.sounds' clock "timer"); a record whose clock is not shown is compared with the offset, and where it differs there the spec stays INCONCLUSIVE

align.name: BN6's battle opening a frame longer
align.what: Every BN4 spec against BN6's (game=bn4:bn6) runs BN6's opening one paused frame longer, BN4's never and no BN5 spec: BN6's plain appear's first blink step counts 3 frames where it counts 2 (its movs r0,#2 at BN6_APPEAR_BLINK_FIRST made movs r0,#3, written into BN6's copy after the install: tools/xdiff_bn4.py alignments, the spec's first poke=). Its one object in the appear queue, the spec's virus, then runs its appear, and the paused present after it (XVirusFamily.present), as many times as BN4's does; the blink ends, the queue empties and bit 1 is set a frame later, so MegaMan's appear ends a frame later too (an object of the side the battle state names, its +0xD against the object's +0x16 at 0x080163C0-0x080163D4, skips the queue and the blink and waits for bit 1): the whole opening a frame longer, its fight frames counted as before. The tool checks BN6's ROM holds `was` there (a movs r0,#imm8) and writes its immediate plus `frames`; a spec of more than one foe is refused (the queue blinks its objects one after another, so a longer first blink step would delay the k-th foe k frames where BN4's bit delays each one)
align.why: The owner's call 7, revised (docs/multirom/bn4.md, The owner's calls): a BN4 visitor keeps BN6's appear and opening in play, and the comparison names the engines' frame between them, as it names BN6's battle a fight frame behind BN4's (allowed, lag 1). Both games' appears run the same steps (BN4_APPEAR 0x0800FE00, BN6_APPEAR 0x08016396, compared SAME by tools/xrecipe_thumb.py but for BN4's battle kind 0x44 and its sound): step 0 into the appear queue (BN4 0x08007F1C, BN6 0x0800AA1A), hidden, waiting for the battle state's appear bit 0 and the queue's head (BN4 0x080019C0 and 0x08007F04, BN6 0x0800139A and 0x0800AA06); step 1 a 2 x 16 frame blink, then out of the queue (BN4 0x08007F46, BN6 0x0800AA40); step 2 waiting for bit 1. Each opening sets bit 0 after its fade, from the same step (BN4 0x080E1F04: bl 0x08005B7C, bne; movs r0,#1; bl BN4_APPEAR_BITS_SET 0x080019A8 at 0x080E1F0E; BN6 0x080E1A04: bl 0x080062F8, bne; movs r0,#1; bl BN6_APPEAR_BITS_SET 0x08001382 at 0x080E1A0E; the fade begun with 0x10 in both, BN4 0x080E1EF4, BN6 0x080E19F4), 18 frames after the virus's init in BN4 (its step 0 run 19 times from its init's frame: frame 132 to 150 in spikey_v1, 131 to 149 in shrimpy_v3) and 17 in BN6 (17 runs from the frame after its init: 71 to 88), the blinks the same 32 frames: a probe of hooks on both, temporary, not kept (docs/rom/bn4.md, A virus's appear and the engine's appear bits). So BN4's virus runs its appear, and its after-state's sprite update, once more in the paused opening than BN6's: 53 after-states before its first fight frame against BN6's 51 and its state 1 (the battle's offset), its sprite a step ahead at t1, and Shrimpy's hook (0x080BA13E: its animation 1 cleared where the one in play has ended, 0x08002E56 bit 0x80) reading its idle animation's last frame a frame earlier, shrimpy_v3 FAIL at t65. The difference is the engines' openings, not the appear's code nor the family's. One paused run more of BN6's appear aligns it: a blink step a frame longer takes the run where a bit 0 a frame later would (the same count of appear runs, bit 1 a frame later), with one immediate of BN6's own appear and no code of the harness's; the bit itself a frame later would need a count the opening's step has not (0x080E1A04-0x080E1A16 sets it the frame the fade ends)
evidence: python3 tools/xdiff.py shrimpy_v3 --poke 080163FC:2003:2 (BN6's first blink step a frame longer) PASS, the opening's allowance then in legit.json unused; without it FAIL at t65 (2026-11-04)

with the alignment every BN4 spec against BN6's PASSES and the opening's allowance and its code (tools/xdiff_bn4.py opening_animation, OPENING_LEAD, anim_steps) are gone; its mutation (tests/xdiff/mutations.json, shrimpy_v3: the first blink step 4 frames, the alignment two) is caught

battle_state.name: a side's wind and its level
battle_state.why: Each side's wind (the fourth kind's 0x41) is kept in the battle state at +0x88 + 4 x side in BN4 and +0xC0 + 4 x side in BN6, its level 8 bytes past it: the slot's setter (BN4 0x080E69C6, BN6 0x080E675A: [r10 +0x18] + 4 x r1 + 0x88 | 0xC0, an old wind there told to end, the new one stored at +0 and r2 at +8) and its reader (BN4 0x080E69E8, BN6 0x080E677C: the same address left in r2, +0 in r0 and +8 in r1) are the same steps but for that constant. The wind's spawn (BN4 0x080E68F8, BN6 0x080E666C) calls the reader and then the fourth kind's spawn (BN4 0x08003344, BN6 0x080033AC), which keeps the caller's r1 to r3 at the object's +0x34 to +0x3C, so the wind's +0x38 points at its side's slot in each game's own place (windman_v1 at t1: +0x8C | +0xC4, WindMan's side 1). A pointer into BN4's battle state between +0x88 and +0x97 is read as BN6's of the same place from +0xC0 (tools/xdiff_snap.py state_off); every other offset of it as it is

ai_data.why: A Soul Navi's own block of his AI data is BN4's +0x64 (BN4_AI_NAVI) and BN6's +0x80 (BN6_AI_NAVI_STATE), where his port moves it (tools/xnavirecipe_bn4.py AI_BLOCKS: each pointer his code makes into it given BN6's offset) and the trace lays BN4's out (src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c ai_segs). A pointer his code keeps to a byte of it is read as BN6's of the same byte: WoodMan's step's callback state (0x080C9178: movs r0,#0xb; adds r0,r0,r6; str r0,[r7,#0x20], r6 his block, BN4 0x080C8F88 adds r6,#0x64 and his copy's #0x80) points at his block's +0xB in both, BN4's AI +0x6F and BN6's +0x8B (woodman_v1 at t1: ai+0xC0 'ai' 111 | 139). A pointer to any other offset of an AI's data is read as it is

ai_data.name: a Soul Navi's attack's variables
ai_data.why: His attack's variables are BN4's +0x70 (BN4_AI_ATTACK_VARS) and BN6's +0xA0 (BN6_AI_ATTACK_VARS), moved and laid out as his own block is (tools/xnavirecipe_bn4.py AI_BLOCKS, src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c ai_segs): a pointer into them is read as BN6's of the same byte

chip_id.why: A chip id where MegaMan's AI data keeps one, BN4's read as the run's: the chip registry's rows for BN4 (a chip of a name of BN4's own takes an id of its own, docs/multirom/chip-registry.md), then the pairs the spec's folders name in the same place (folder4[i], folder6[i]: a chip both games name is BN6's own, paired by name as pair_bn4 pairs it). The place: his AttackVars +0x14, the chip used, written by the chip's use in both (BN4 0x0800D4D2 and BN6 0x08012824 / 0x080126F6: strh r0,[r7,#0x14], r7 the AI data + 0xA0). And his attack's subfamily (AttackVars +3), which each game's use copies from the chip's record +0x0C (BN4 0x0800D510-0x0800D512 and BN6 0x0801271A-0x0801271C: ldrb r1,[rec,#0xc]; strb r1,[r7,#3]): the two games number their support family's subfamilies apart (BN4's 0x0C/0x11 the time bomb's, BN6's 0x15/0x0A; BN4's table 0x080220E0, BN6's 0x0802CCB4), so where the run's chip is one of BN6's own and BN4's byte is its chip's record's, it is read as BN6's record's. A support chip's object keeps the chip too (support_objects, below). Not a mask: a subfamily that is not the record's, or a chip no row and no folder pairs, is compared as it is.
chip_id.record_why: What each game's use copies of the chip's record into MegaMan's AttackVars beside the subfamily (BN4 0x0800D508-0x0800D51A: the record's +0x0A to +0xA, its +0x10 word to +0xC, its +0x14 to +5; BN6 0x080126FE-0x08012714: the +0x10 word to +0xC, +0x0A above the power in the word at +8, +0x14 to +5), and the power at +8 where it is the record's own (+0x1A, no boost on it): for a chip both games name, which a run plays as BN6's with BN6's record, the two records are not one (HolyPanl's first parameter 6 in BN4's and 4 in BN6's, Barrier's 0 and 1, LifeAura's 5 and LifeAur's 9: BN4's routines map theirs through tables of its own; a chip that deals no damage holds 0x28 at BN4's power and 0 at BN6's), so each copy that is BN4's record's bytes is read as BN6's record's. Only for a pair whose BN6 chip is BN6's own (an id under 411): a registry row's record is made from BN4's and is compared as it is. The record's +0x0A goes on from there: the support run hands it above the power (r6), the support object's spawn keeps it at +0x2E, a third-kind object it spawns takes the same word, and that object's collision set-up copies its byte (BN6 0x08019FD8-0x08019FDA: ldrh r3,[r5,#0x2e]; strb r3,[r7,#7]; BN4 0x080129C6-0x080129C8 to its +5, the trace's layout BN6's). So a third-kind object whose damage word is BN4's record's power and +0x0A reads its +0x2E, and its collision data's copy, as BN6's record's (RockCube's cube: 0x32 in BN4's record 99, 0x9E in BN6's 143; bn4_chip_rockcube t34).
evidence: bn4_chip_timebomb t32: MegaMan's AttackVars +0x14 0x61 in BN4's (its TimeBomb, 97) and 0x90 in BN6's (TimeBom1, 144, the spec's folders' pair); +3 0x11 in BN4's (record 97's +0x0C) and 0x0A in BN6's (record 144's +0x0C)
bn4_chip_areagrab t33: the area grab's object's +0x30 0x75 in BN4's (AreaGrab, 117) and 0xA3 in BN6's (163)

megaman_misc_wait.why: BN4's misc run waits after one subfamily's routine before it ends the attack (BN4_MISC_WAIT 0x080EC9AC: cmp r0,#5; movs r0,#0x28; strh r0,[r7,#0x10], counted down a frame each, bgt at 0x080EC9BA): SidBmbo's 0x28 frames. BN6's run waits for its own subfamily 0x14 alone (0x080ED712), so the unit's entry in BN6's grown misc routines is a wrapper of the installer's (src/emu/xchips_code.c wait_stage, XChipUnit.wait) that is the run's routine every frame of the wait: it calls the unit's routine once, sets the count to BN4's and counts it as BN4's run does, ending the attack through BN6's run (BN6_MISC_END 0x080ED722) at 0. The count (the state's +0x10) holds BN4's numbers each frame and is compared as ever. The state's phase halfword is each run's own bookkeeping while it waits: BN4's run marks its phase 4 (movs r0,#4; strb r0,[r7] at 0x080EC982-0x080EC984) and comes back to its count-down by it (bne at 0x080EC980); BN6's run marks 1 (0x080ED6E8-0x080ED6EA), which the wrapper clears each frame it goes on waiting so that the run calls it again (its strb at +0x2C), keeping a mark of its own in the halfword's second byte (its strb at +0x16: the routine called once), a byte an attack's set clears with the phase (BN6 0x080116A4: strh r0,[r1]). So BN4's 0x0004 there is read as BN6's 0x0100, only in BN4's misc state (his CurAction 0x20), only with BN4's phase 4 and a second byte of 0, and only where his attack's subfamily is a unit's that waits (src/emu/xchips_bn4.c's rows with a wait). bn4_chip_sidbmbo1: t33 to t71 in BN4's, the attack ended at t72 in BN4's and t73 in BN6's (the battle's offset), the count 0x27 down to 1 in both

navi_chips.why: A BN4 Navi chip whose Navi is moved (a unit of kind navi, tools/xchiprecipe_bn4_navi.py; src/emu/xchips_bn4.c's XCHIP_NAVI rows) runs in BN6's engine as BN6's Navi chips do, and is read so. Its family: BN4 runs its Navi chips by its support state (MegaMan's state 0x0C, 0x080EB9EA: the chip's routine of the table 0x080220E0 by its subfamily, then the attack's end in the same frame), BN6 by a family of their own, 0x1B (0x080ED690: its Navi chip object's spawner 0x080E2C6C with the subfamily in r3, the same registers handed on, then the attack's end in the same frame, where its support family 0x15 holds MegaMan a frame more: megaman_clock). The chip's registry row is XREG_MOVED and names a BN6 Navi chip as the twin whose family its record takes (src/core/xchips_record.c xrec_from_bn4; BN6's Roll, 221), its subfamily the unit's number in BN6's grown Navi routines. So where the chip in MegaMan's AI data (chip_id's place) is such a row's, BN4's state 0x0C is read as that twin's record's family, read from BN6's ROM. Its object: BN4's routine spawns a fourth-kind object of the Navi's own (GutsMan's type 0x10, 0x080E31E8), BN6's spawner its one Navi chip object (type 0x10, 0x080E2B28), the same four states (tools/xchiprecipe_bn4_navi.py OBJECTS, each BN4 object read against BN6's): BN4's object, found as the type the unit's routine of BN4's support table spawns (the common spawner's shape, support_objects), is read as BN6's type 0x10; its element at BN6's +0x0E (BN4's spawner stores r3 at +0x17, BN6's at +0x0E); the spawn's leftover r3 at +0x3C, BN4's routine's own address (the support run's bx r3) and BN6's the subfamily (0x080ED696: ldrb r3,[r7,#3]), as the unit's number, and BN6's copy of it at +0x19 (0x080E2C98-0x080E2C9A: ldr r1,[r0,#0x3c]; strb r1,[r0,#0x19]), which no code of BN4's object reads or writes; and the chip at +0x30 as the run's id. Not a mask: an object of another type, or one whose +0x3C is not its routine's address, is compared as it is.
evidence: bn4_chip_gutsman t32: MegaMan's CurAction BN4 0x0C, BN6 0x1B, the frame the chip is used in both
bn4_chip_gutsman t33: the object's +0x19 0 and 0x85, +0x3C 0x080E3305 (BN4's routine) and 0x85

megaman_lockout.why: As a chip's attack ends each game keeps the chip's lock-out (the record's +0x14, MegaMan's AttackVars +5) in his AI data, the frames he cannot act: BN4's end stores it as a halfword at +0x3A (0x0800C9FC: ldrb r0,[r7,#5]; strh r0,[r1,#0x3a] at 0x0800CA0A-0x0800CA0C), BN6's as a byte at +0x19 (0x08011714: ldrb r0,[r7,#5]; strb r0,[r1,#0x19] at 0x08011732-0x08011734, for an attack of kind 2), each counted down a frame at a time. BN4's is read at BN6's place where BN6's place holds 0 in BN4's AI data and the halfword's high byte is 0. bn4_chip_counter1 t58: 0x1D at BN4's +0x3A and at BN6's +0x19 (Counter1's 30 frames, one counted).

attack_families.why: MegaMan's CurAction while he uses a chip is the chip's family in both games: BN4's a state of his (BN4_PLAYER_STATES 0x080EAEFC by the record's +0xB, run with his object in r5; the state makes r7 the attack's variables itself, his AI data's +0x70: the spread family's 0x080EC762-0x080EC764), BN6's an attack family (BN6_ATTACK_FAMILIES 0x080EBFA0 by the number less 0x10, run by RunAIAttack with r7 the variables, his AI data's +0xA0: BN6's twin family 0x25 reads them at 0x080EDEF4 with no load of its own). A unit of BN4's chips' code of the kind 'attack' is one of BN4's states moved whole into BN6's grown attack families at a number of BN4's chips' own (src/emu/xattack_grow.h XATTACK_BN4, 0xD0 on; tools/xchiprecipe_bn4.py ATTACK_NUMBERS), which its chips' records take as their family with BN4's own subfamily (src/core/xchips_record.c xrec_from_bn4). So BN4's family in his CurAction and in the action his saved state keeps is read as that number, by the units' rows (XCHIP_ATTACK, BN4's family, the number); his attack's subfamily is BN4's own in both and is left as it is (a registry row whose `sub` is 0xD0 or over names the family, not a support routine).

megaman_animations.why: MegaMan's sprite is each game's own art ("MegaMan's own sprite"), and the two number his animations otherwise. A state of BN4's sets the one it runs by a store to his object's +0x10 (and 0xFF to +0x11, which the sprite update makes the animation run; his sprite state keeps it at +0x90); BN6's twin family sets BN6's number of the same animation through 0x0800F2B6, which stores it and 0xFF likewise. A moved state's store is given BN6's number by its recipe's immediate (tools/xchiprecipe_bn4.py IMMS, each from the two twin families' code), so BN4's number and BN6's differ where the two battles run one animation. Read as the same only while his CurAction is the moved family's in both, only for the pairs listed, each with both games' sites; the frames run of the animation are compared as ever ("MegaMan's own art's animation")

interrupted_attack.why: An attack's state sets 0x400000 in MegaMan's collision flags as it begins and the attack's end clears it, in both games (the spread family's state: BN4 0x080EC7B2-0x080EC7B6, movs r0,#1; lsls r0,#22; bl 0x08012F82, its end 0x0800C9FC's bl 0x08012F8C at 0x0800CA16; BN6's twin family 0x25 at 0x080EDF38-0x080EDF3C, bl 0x0801A152, its end 0x08011714's bl 0x0801A15C at 0x08011750). Where a hit ends the attack instead, the two engines' struck states part: BN6's (his state 3, 0x080174FE) sets 0x400400 as it begins and clears both bits as it ends (0x0801758A: bl 0x0801A15C), so the attack's bit goes with it; BN4's (0x08010960) sets and clears 0x400 alone (0x0801096C-0x08010970, 0x080109DE-0x080109E2), so the attack's bit stands until his next attack ends (the same two states "BN6's MegaMan's paralysis state's flag 0x400000" names, from BN6's side). His struck state in BN6's engine is BN6's own, not the moved unit's. Guarded: that bit alone, BN4's holding it and BN6's not, only while his CurAction is a generic state's in both games (BN4's 6 or under, BN6's 8 or under: in an attack's state the bit is compared as ever, so a moved state that did not set it fails), every other bit of the word compared as ever. bn4_chip_heatshot_struck: HeatShot used at fight frame 88, MegaMan struck by the Mettaur's wave at t97 with his arm out; the bit differs from t120, as his struck state ends, to the spec's end

actor_objects.why: A third-kind object both engines run by the actors' state runner (BN4 0x08013F3E, BN6 0x0801B394, each with the object's own state table): its CurAction (+9) numbers its own states from 6 in BN4 and from 8 in BN6, as a first-kind object's does (BN4's generic states 0-5, BN6's 0-7: tools/bn4_twins.py GENERIC4), so BN4's from 6 are read two higher. By type, each with its two state tables.

T3.0x59: RockCube's cube: its update calls the runner with its table (BN4 0x080D8AA6: ldr r0,=0x080D8ABC, seven states, its own the first, the third and the seventh; BN6 0x080D12A2: ldr r0,=0x080D12B8, nine, its own the first, the third and the ninth). bn4_chip_rockcube t34: +9 6 in BN4's and 8 in BN6's, the cube standing

support_objects.why: A support chip's object, the fourth kind's type its subfamily's routine spawns, holds what its spawn copied of the caller's registers: every such spawner has one shape in both games (push {lr}; push {r0,r1,r2,r5}; movs r0,#type; the fourth kind's spawn, BN4 0x08003344 and BN6 0x080033AC; then str r6,[r0,#0x2c]; str r7,[r0,#0x30]), reached by bx r3 from each game's support run (BN4 0x080EB9EA from the table 0x080220E0, BN6 0x080ED0DC from 0x0802CCB4) with r3 the spawner's own address, r4 the attack's parameters ([r7,#0xc]), r6 its power word ([r7,#8]) and r7 the chip and the attack's +6. So the object's +4 holds the parameters (the spawn's store of r4), +0x2C the power word, +0x30 the chip, and +0x3C each game's address of its spawner (the spawn's store of r1 to r3 at +0x34 to +0x3C). Read in BN6's terms where all of this is so, checked against both ROMs at each run (tools/xdiff_bn4.py support_spawners: the type's spawner of that shape in each game's table, and no routine of the type, down its jump tables, loading +0x3C): BN4's +0x3C, where it is its spawner's address, as BN6's spawner's of the run's chip's subfamily; the chip as the run's id (chip_id); and for a chip both games name the record's copies as BN6's record's (chip_id's record). A type whose spawner is another shape, or whose code loads +0x3C, is compared as it is. A chip whose code is BN4's moved (its row XREG_MOVED: PanlSht's fourth kind's 0x4F, ShotStar's 0x34, src/emu/xchips_bn4.c) has no spawner in BN6's ROM: its spawner is BN4's of that shape, the unit's entry, whose copy BN6's support run calls. Its object's chip is read as the run's id all the same; its +0x3C, the same routine's address in both, BN6's its copy read back as BN4's address by the trace's moved ranges, is compared as the number it is; and its element, which the spawner stores from r3 at BN4's +0x17 (BN4 0x080E7A6C: strb r3,[r0,#0x17]) and the recipe's immediate at BN6's +0x0E, is read at BN6's place where BN4's +0x0E holds 0 (bn4_chip_shotstar t33: 1 at BN4's +0x17 and at BN6's +0x0E).

An animation a state sets in the fight (his paralysis's at t431, t520 in BN4 and t432, t521 in BN6) starts a count a frame behind with it, compared with the battle's offset A moved Navi's own the same (GutsMan's in gutsman_v1: his appear's animation set in the opening, 1 at t1 in both, then his state's at BN4's t2 and BN6's t3): his after-step, run after each of his states (BN4 0x080143FC, BN6's twin 0x0801BBAC, the same body but for the pause test's routine, BN4 0x080078EC, BN6 0x0800A03C), runs the sprite update (BN4 0x0800285C, BN6 0x080026C4) at every fight frame and at none of the paused opening's, so his opening animation's count is the frame's clock too; a moved family's own needs no rule, its paused present (XVirusFamily.present) animating it as BN4's after-state does
