companion_clock.name: a Navi's companion's animation from the opening, by the fight's frames

objects.what: AquaMan's companion (kind 1) and WindMan's (kinds 2 and 3), BN4_T1_COMPANION

companion_clock.why: A BN4 Navi's companion's sprite state (its sprite's +0 to +0x2B: the animation, its count, flags, art and frame), the first kind's type his recipe moves (its role told by its type, tools/xdiff_snap.py T1_MOVED), until it first steps with the battle's offset. AquaMan's companion (the first kind's 0x5C, kind 1, spawned by his init at 0x080B826A, in BN6 at his spawn's end) sets its animation up in its init (0x080CCCDC, the animation setter BN4 0x08002E10, BN6 0x08002DA4), in the battle's paused opening. Its update (0x080CCD3C, run every frame by the object runner, its +0 0x04 from its spawner, 0x080CCF4A) runs its mode 8 (0x080CCE8C), which runs its kind's routine (kind 1's 0x080CCECC) and then the after-step (BN4 0x080143FC at 0x080CCEB0, unless time is stopped, 0x08007948 at 0x080CCEAA); its copy in BN6 calls the twins (BN6 0x0801BBAC and 0x0800A098, tools/bn4_twins.py), whose pause tests (BN4 0x080078EC, BN6 0x0800A03C) skip the sprite update (BN4 0x0800285C, BN6 0x080026C4) in the paused opening and run it at every fight frame from the first. So its animation runs by the fight's frames, the second clock (bn4 clocks), not by its Navi's state runner (BN4 0x08013C48, BN6 0x0801B1C4), which BN6 opens a frame later (allowed, "BN6's battle a fight frame behind BN4's"). It is set up again only from its Navi's state: kind 1's routine marks its +0xC while AquaMan's animation (his +0x10) is not 0 (0x080CCED0-0x080CCEE0) and, once it is 0 again, clears it and makes its +0x11 0xFF (0x080CCEE4-0x080CCEF0), so the after-step sets its animation up anew (0x0801442C-0x0801443E) and it follows the battle's offset from there. In aquaman_v1 its count reads 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 2, 1 at BN4's t1-t10 and at BN6's t1-t10, a frame ahead at the offset, and from BN4's t11 (BN6's t12), its animation set up again, the same at the offset. Compared at the same fight frame (BN6's record of BN4's t) until its sprite state is first the same at the battle's offset, exactly from then on (tools/xdiff_bn4_opening.py CompanionClock); any other difference fails the spec. FireMan's companion (0x57) copies his animation from his first state on (companion_opening_count) and is not held

opening_animation.name: an animation run through the paused opening, by the openings' lengths
opening_animation.why: A moved object's sprite state (its sprite's +0 to +0x2B: the animation, its count, flags, art and frame) while no animation was set in the fight (its +0x90 and +0x11 as at its first fight frame in both games). ThunderMan's cloud (the third kind's 0x6A, spawned by his companion's init, 0x080C3B26) sets its animation in its init, in the battle's set-up (0x080DAACE, the animation setter BN4 0x08002E10, BN6 0x08002DA4), and its type routine (0x080DAA90) runs the third kind's after-state after its update every frame it runs (BN4 0x080144FE, BN6 0x0801BCA6, the same body: the sprite update, BN4 0x0800285C, BN6 0x080026C4, with no pause test), which both object runners do through the paused opening, its +0 having 0x04 (0x17 from its spawn in both: BN4 0x0800314C at 0x08003174, BN6 0x080031AC at 0x080031D8; its update clears it only once the fight runs, 0x080DAB36). The openings are not the same length: a probe of hooks on both cores (temporary, not kept) in thunderman_v1 saw the cloud spawned at the set-up's last frame and animated every frame to the fight, BN4's 227 frames to its first fight frame (the appear 52, phase 4 one, the Custom screen 122, BATTLE START! 51) and BN6's 206 (52, one, 87, 65): each engine's banner its own length, each game's Custom screen passed by the harness's keys as its window opens (src/dev/xdiff.c). So each game's cloud enters the fight at its own place in its animation (an 18-frame loop of six frames, 4, 2, 4, 2, 4, 2), BN4's 21 frames further on. Compared by that place (tools/xdiff_bn4_opening.py, Opening.phase): the same animation, of the same frames in all, each game's frames run of it as far apart as the frames each ran since its spawn (its spawn event's core frame to its first fight record's, and the fight's frames to the record compared, BN6's at the battle's offset), modulo the animation's frames, read from BN4's bytes of its sprite (BN6's copy the same bytes); any other place fails the spec, and from an animation set in the fight on (the cloud's at t12 in BN4, t13 in BN6) its sprite state is compared exactly

opening_draws.what: A family's draws before the fight, made each unpaused frame of the opening before the appear's bit 0, paired from the opening's end: where BN4's made more of a key's than BN6's, the battle is run again with BN6's k-th setup draw of the key given BN4's (k + N)-th, BN4's first N left without a twin (tools/xdiff_bn4.py opening_skips, the spec's setupskip=KEY:N, src/dev/xdiff_events.c replay_setup). N is bounded, never the gap of the counts: it must equal BN4's draws of the key in the two unpaused frames BN6's opening has no twin of, read from BN4's trace by frame (twinless_draws: the family object's init frame, its spawn's, and the frame before the appear's bit 0, the frame before BN4_APPEAR's step 0 plays its sound as it sees the bit); where the gap is any other number (a draw of BN6's dropped or added), nothing is paired so and the spec runs as it is, failing where the family's state parts. BN6's count of them must be the same in both runs, else INCONCLUSIVE. Every other setup draw keeps the reference's k-th (Shrimpy's and Spikey's one draw in their init, the same count in both).
opening_draws.why: The engines' openings differ by two unpaused frames before the appear's bit 0, the two the opening's alignment (align, BN6's battle opening a frame longer) and the battle's offset (allowed, lag 1) name: BN4's family runs its update in its init's frame (its type routine's init ends in the update) and BN4 sets bit 0 18 frames after the init, BN6 17, BN6's hook 3 running from the frame after the init. A family whose update's own step draws every such frame draws two more in BN4: MagTect's shake (BN4 0x080BF064, entered as hook 3 from 0x080BEBF6: unless the battle is paused, 0x08007948, or the can-move check's third form says not, 0x0800AD7E, and while its +0x20 is a multiple of 4, its offsets +0x36 and +0x3E moved to a random pair of its table's bytes, kept at +0x64 and +0x68) draws at BN4's frames 132-149 (18, the first in its init's frame) and BN6's 72-87 (16) in magtect_v1, the same counts in v2 and v3. Each shake sets its offsets from that draw alone (+0x64 the new byte, +0x36 moved by new less old), so the state the fight begins with is the last draw's: paired k-th with k-th, BN6's last takes BN4's sixteenth number where BN4's last took its eighteenth (magtect_v1 FAIL at t1 on +0x36, +0x64 and +0x9C); paired from the opening's end, BN6's sixteen take BN4's last sixteen, the frames before bit 0 the same steps of the appear's wait in both. Not the family's code: its copy runs BN4's shake whole, the engine deciding how many frames it runs before the fight.
